title: fix(app,ui): name the setup carry's turn, stop counting dialog time as a freeze
body:
Fork synced at v0.17.0. Effort: high (no escalation).

## Root causes (#866)

1. **The carry refusal is correct by design, not a frame bug.** The viewport draws the active setup's frame, so the plate standing upright in Setup2 means the plate is modelled lying flat and Setup2 holds it turned X -90° (a part-alignment change on Setup2; `CreateSetup` itself never sets one - with "Carry stock and WCS over" it copies Setup1's). Setup1 holds it as modelled, so the turn *between* the setups is a real side-on quarter turn about X, which the column lattice of the carried stock cannot re-index (`CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL`). `setup_relative::transform_between` already composes `A_to * A_from^-1` (the relative turn): two setups holding the part alike - both turned X -90° - carry fine, now pinned. The unpicked stock source of a setup that holds the part differently defaults to the carry (#317's rule), which is why the refused option shows selected but disabled. Lifting the limit is filed as **#874** (effort:max, after the field engine #637 / #586).
2. **The "35 s freeze" was the user's time in the file dialog.** The native dialogs (rfd) are modal and synchronous and open from `State::drain_actions`, inside the frame's "commands" phase; the frame watch (#74) counted the browsing time as app work. The log's xdg-desktop-portal warning (the dialog opening) sits right before the slow frame; the STEP tessellates off-thread as before. (**#872**)
3. **Jargon** - "furniture" is our in-code word for a setup's stock, WCS and fixtures; the refusal text named neither the turn nor a way out. (**#873**)

## What changed
- `crates/app/src/stock_sim_carry.rs`: a turn refusal names the relative turn, "'Setup2' holds the part turned X -90°, Y 0°, Z 0° from how 'Setup1' holds it, and <CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL>".
- `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/carry.rs`: `CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL` kept by name, reworded: "the stock simulation can carry machined stock only through a flip over X or Y or a quarter turn about Z (turns that keep the tool axis vertical) - any other turn would have to re-sample the stock and lose its detail".
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/setup_stock_pick.rs`: the page says what happened and what to do - choose "Its own stock", or hold the part as the previous setup does (a flip over X/Y or a turn about Z also works).
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/setup_pages.rs`, `pages.rs`: the radio reads "Active setup - new operations go into it, and the Stock and Work offset pages edit it"; the Setups page footer drops "furniture".
- `crates/ui/src/file_dialog.rs`, `frame_watch.rs`, `shell_window/frame.rs`: every modal dialog is timed (`file_dialog::take_waited`) and the frame watch takes that time off the frame (`FrameWatch::excuse`); work beyond the wait is still reported.
- `docs/decisions/866-setup2-carry.md`.

## How tested
Pinning tests (all pass locally on macOS, clippy `-D warnings` clean on sim/app/ui):
- `setup_stock_source::both_setups_turned_alike_carry_through_the_identity` - the relative-turn composition.
- `setup_stock_source::a_side_on_turn_between_setups_is_refused_naming_the_turn` - the refusal names the turn and keeps `CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL`.
- `egui_app::frame_watch::tests::time_in_a_modal_dialog_is_not_a_slow_frame`.
- `egui_app::setup_stock_tests::the_settings_page_has_no_in_code_jargon`; `a_refused_carry_disables_the_option_with_its_reason` extended with the turn and the way out.
- Re-ran `setup_carry`, `carried_verify`, `camcraft-sim stock_carry` (they match on `CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL`): green.
- Linux quick gate: see the comment below.

## Not exercised
- The reporter's own STEP file (not attached); reproduced with a flat plate mesh turned X -90° in Setup2.
- A live run of a native file dialog (the timing seam is pinned at the frame-watch level; the dialog itself is not driven in tests).
- Snapshot PNGs untouched (release lane).

Changelog: The setup page names the turn that stops the stock carry and says what to do, drops the "furniture" jargon, and the slow-frame log no longer blames time spent in a file dialog (#866, #872, #873)

Fixes #872
Fixes #873
Refs #866

title: fix(adaptive): bound the growth planner by the geometry it works, not only path length
body:
## What changed

The growth-ring planner (`adaptive/grow.rs`) was bounded only by #13's length budget (revolution length in tool radii). Its time goes into whole-ring polygon work on every trial step, and that work per tool radius depends on the shape. On the island fixture it ran ~53 s (release, this machine; the issue measured ~68 s) before the length budget refused it.

A third budget law in `adaptive/budget.rs` (`Work`, `GEOM_MAX`) now counts the **polygon vertices each trial step works through**: the cleared area it offsets, the ring it opens, and each revolution's margin area. The count is summed over every margin attempt, like the length budget. Past **500,000** vertices the plan is refused by name:

> adaptive: the HSM plan is refused: growing the cleared area ran past its planning budget after 88 revolutions - its rings (~502 k outline vertices worked, over 500 k) are too detailed to plan in seconds (an island?); a trochoid ... - Offset rings cut this pocket instead

- **Deterministic, no wall clock.** The same project plans, or is refused, on every machine and under any load. No wall-clock backstop was added: the vertex bound already caps the time.
- **Fallback unchanged.** The refusal uses the existing `refused` path, so `pocket_hsm`'s named trochoid -> Offset-ring fallback is the same and the island's fallback output is identical (162 moves, same report line).
- **Length budgets unchanged.** `LEAST_WORK_MAX` and `WORK_MAX` did not need to move.
- `mod.rs` stays at 435 lines: the `Cell<f64>` field became `budget::Work`.
- Counters use saturating arithmetic. No unwrap, expect or panic outside tests.

**Why vertices.** Trial count does not separate the cases: the island and the slot both spend ~550 trials. The up-front estimate does not either: the island reads 339 r and the slot 113 r, both far under 2,000. Time follows vertex count to within ~2x. Full reasoning and the dropped options are in `docs/decisions/850-adaptive-geometry-budget.md`.

## Calibration (deterministic counts, measured with a local probe that is not committed)

| fixture (suite) | ends | vertices | share of 500 k |
|---|---|---|---|
| 60 x 14 slot (`adaptive_hsm` pocket) | Done | 252,328 | 0.50 |
| 60 x 14 slot (`adaptive::tests` plan) | Done | 246,290 | 0.49 |
| 60 x 22 channel (`adaptive_hsm`) | Done (then trochoid/rings, unchanged) | 175,217 | 0.35 |
| whole_model_pocket, largest corner | Done | 73,496 | 0.15 |
| motion level_links | Done | 37,545 | 0.08 |
| pocket_overhead / machining2d | Done | 34,508 | 0.07 |
| 14 / 20 mm band, shoulder_adaptive | refused up front (#13) | 0 | - |
| island 60 x 40, 12 x 12 | **refused** after 88 revs | 502,660 | > 1 |

Before this change the island spent 865 k vertices in its first margin attempt, and 1.95 M in its second before the length budget refused it. Margin: every fixture that grows today stays at least **1.98x** under the budget, pinned at 1.9x.

## Bound in seconds (this machine, the whole island pocket: growth, trochoid refusal, Offset rings)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| island, release | 52.6 s | **19.0 s** |
| island, debug | not measured (well over a minute by the same ratio) | **38.7 s** |
| 14 mm band, release | 0.14 s (refused up front) | same |

## Pinning tests

1. `adaptive_hsm::the_island_is_refused_by_the_geometry_budget_in_seconds` (default lane, ~39 s debug). Checks:
   - the refusal is named;
   - the vertex count in the note lies in 500..=520 k, so it was refused within one revolution of the budget (deterministic);
   - the Offset rings cut the pocket, chained and finite;
   - **the verifier is silent** on them (solid law included);
   - a loose wall-clock backstop: 600 s debug, 60 s release.
2. `adaptive::tests::a_channel_is_grown_as_one_spiral_that_never_crosses` (existing debug test) now also asserts that the slot's plan spends at most 1/1.9 of the budget.
3. `adaptive::budget::fixtures::the_fixtures_that_grow_today_stay_under_the_geometry_budget`: the slot and channel pockets, 1.9x margin. It runs ~140 s in debug, so it is `#[ignore]`d into the heavy lane (release `--ignored`).
4. `adaptive::budget::tests::the_geometry_budget_refuses_by_name_and_saturates`: the `Work` unit test (refusal names, saturation, and that NaN length is ignored).

## Gate

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: **green** (motion lib + adaptive_band + adaptive_hsm + pocket3d_hsm, 103 s).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- With the budget compiled in, these debug suites all passed:
  - motion: lib, adaptive_band, adaptive_hsm, level_links, machining2d, machining3d, pocket3d_hsm, rotary_adaptive, rotary_dflat;
  - app: pick_agnostic, pocket_overhead, pocket3d_hsm, probe_op, project_roundtrip, roughing2d, shoulder_adaptive, stock_engine_agreement, whole_model_pocket, level_links.
- Release: the new island pin and `hsm_one` (island) were run; the island's fallback report line is unchanged.

**Goldens.** No committed `.cl`/`.nc` golden is an adaptive pocket. Every plan that finished before still finishes with the same count path. The length check is evaluated first, so a plan refused by length keeps its old message. The code path only adds a counter and a check at each revolution start.

## Not exercised

- **Heavy lanes that run Adaptive, not run (per the brief):**
  - `rotary_adaptive` (three ignored tests on the developed bar);
  - motion `pocket3d_hsm::the_stepped_block_...`;
  - app `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_...`;
  - `adaptive_hsm::hsm_report_full_resolution`.

  Their growth counts are unmeasured. If one of them now reads "too detailed" where it planned before, that is a regression to report: please run those lanes in the review or at the cut. This is the main residual risk.
- The new heavy-lane margin test itself was not run with `--ignored` (its two pockets' counts are the measured 252 k / 175 k above, taken from the same code).
- The debug "before" time for the island.

## What this means for #845

#845's held fix (`issue/7-r10-corner-reading`) roughly doubles growth work.
- **Island:** it would now be refused at the same 500 k vertices, in the same ~19 s, instead of running even longer. The bound holds.
- **Slot:** it spends 252 k today, so a doubling would put it at or over the budget. #845 must re-measure the slot and channel counts. If they cross 500 k, it raises `GEOM_MAX` with numbers (the pin in `budget_fixtures.rs` and `adaptive::tests` will tell it), rather than refusing the slot.

Effort: high (no escalation).

Changelog: Adaptive: the growth planner is now also bounded by the polygon geometry it works through (deterministic), so an islanded area it cannot finish is refused by name in seconds (island fixture ~19 s instead of ~1 min) before the named Offset-ring fallback

Fixes #850

title: fix(mcp): locate_part takes mate ids by the one pick rule; what a click picks (#692)
body:
The remaining part of #692, after #705 (feature graph + pick API) and #709 (every viewport picker on the rule).

## Audit
The full table is on the issue: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/692#issuecomment-6801617642. In short, on main bdd29e00 every point of the issue was met and pinned except three:

| Point | Before | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| MCP `locate_part` mate ids | bypassed the rule: `fixture_tools::locate_part` parsed ids with `parse_feature_id` and never called `check_pickable`, so a vertex along a round rim or inside a face became a mate point | runs `pick::check_pickable` like every other MCP pick (`mcp::pick::pick_of`); refused by name |
| User docs note on what a click picks | missing | new "What a click picks" section in `site/content/guide/operations.md` |
| Circle/arc centre picks | the API's centre tier, no page asks for it | **waits for #759** (draft); not touched |

Everything else (faces, feature edges, feature points, hidden geometry, perspective/ortho, snap order by the tool's kinds, every UI picker incl. fixture locate, MCP list/set picks, degenerate input) is already pinned by `feature_pick::*`, `feature_pick_wire::*`, `one_pick_rule::*` and `mcp_pick::listed_chains_and_vertices_follow_the_one_pick_rule` - names in the audit table.

## What changed
- `crates/app/src/mcp/fixture_tools.rs`: `locate_part` checks each mate id with `pick::check_pickable` (3 lines).
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_pick.rs`: pinning test `locate_part_refuses_a_mate_point_no_click_could_pick`; the boss STL writer is now a helper shared with `listed_chains_and_vertices_follow_the_one_pick_rule`.
- `site/content/guide/operations.md`: "What a click picks".
- `docs/decisions/692-pick-rule-rest.md`: why the check sits at the MCP door, why no pick-through control in the viewport, why centres wait for #759.

## How tested
- Pinning test `mcp_pick::locate_part_refuses_a_mate_point_no_click_could_pick`: FAILS with the fix stashed, passes with it.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on 3af6e765: green (app lib, mcp_pick, mcp_setup - 29 s).
- By name: `feature_pick` 7/7, `feature_pick_wire` 4/4 (1 timing lane ignored), `mcp_pick` 4/4, UI `egui_app::tests::one_pick_rule` 6/6 (CWD crates/ui).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. No UI code changed.

## Not exercised
- The maintainer's hand GUI check of the viewport picks (#709's note) - no GUI was launched; the UI behaviour is pinned by `one_pick_rule::*`.
- No pick-through control is offered in the viewport (decision record); the API's `through` flag is pinned by `feature_pick::pick_through_does_pick_the_far_side_edge`.

Changelog: MCP `locate_part` refuses a mate id no click could pick (a vertex along a round edge or inside a face), like the other pick tools; the user guide says what a click picks.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Refs #692 - centre picks wait for #759; the issue closes with that PR or by the maintainer after the hand GUI check.

title: feat(ui): a refused generation shows the moves it had built as a ghost
body:
## What changed

#261 part 3 (parts 1 and 2 shipped in PR #349 and PRs #678/#684): a refused generation now shows the moves the generator had built when it refused, as a **display-only diagnostic ghost**.

- **Carrier (one channel, part 2's).** `GenError` gets a `Ghosted { msg, at, ghost }` variant (`with_ghost`, `ghost()`, `map_ghost`, `map_msg`, `without_ghost`). It reads exactly like the plain refusal, so no message changes. The new type `machining2d::Ghost` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/ghost.rs`) is bounded at 100 000 moves (it sets `truncated` when capped) and never holds a non-finite move. Its `Debug` prints only its size. `CommandError::MachiningGhost` carries the ghost in world coordinates: a 3+2 tilt maps it through the same `world_path` as a real path. The UI keeps it in `State::feedback_ghost` and reads it only through `State::refusal_ghost()`, which uses the same lifecycle law as part 2's `refusal_focus`.
- **Viewport.** `crates/ui/src/refusal_ghost.rs` draws the ghost dashed in the palette's gouge colour, dimmed (rapids dimmer still), with no chevrons, under part 2's spot cross. The only edit to the large files is one call in `interact::toolpath_lines`.
- **Never a toolpath.** The ghost rides the error only. It is never written to the operation, so nothing caches, simulates, verifies or posts it. It is freed when the refusal retires: on the next command (a regeneration included) or an edit of the draft.
- **Script / MCP.** The `generate` error adds the ghost's move count ("a partial path of N move(s) was built before the refusal; it is not kept"). The moves themselves are not included.

### Generators that carry a ghost
- The ladders' centre-cutting refusal (`approach::refusal` on the finished builder): 2D Pocket / Adaptive / Offset, Contour (rings and open chains), Slot (both kinds), Bore, Circular, and the 3-D ladder (Pocket3D, Multi-Axis Rough).
- The plunge law's after-the-fact audit (`plunge_law::audit*`): the 3-D finish and multiaxis centre-cut guards, Rotary Offset's bar audit, the posed audit (Multi-Axis Rough) and the facer's air-entry fallback. Here the ghost is the whole audited path, shown beside part 2's spot.

### Generators that carry none (by design, listed in `docs/decisions/261-refusal-ghost.md`)
- Refusals raised before anything is built: parameter doors, drilling, the bore and thread-mill hole doors, region and tool gates.
- Rotary Offset's wrap-space ladder drops its ghost (`without_ghost`). Its moves live in the development, not where the part is.
- Generators that return before `finish()`. Getting a path out of them would mean restructuring them.

## Pins
- **No toolpath, no post, no sim:** `refusal_ghost::an_op_with_a_ghost_has_no_toolpath_and_the_post_and_the_sim_refuse_it` (app). After a refused generation that carries a ghost: `toolpath_of` is `None`, the status is `Never`, `posting::program_ops` says "SLT: no toolpath yet", and `stock_sim::simulate_document` refuses.
- `refusal_ghost::a_refused_slot_hands_back_its_built_moves_in_world`, `a_centre_cutting_tool_generates_the_slot_and_carries_no_ghost`, `the_script_and_mcp_refusal_names_the_ghosts_size_not_its_moves` (app).
- `refusal_ghost_tests::a_refused_generation_draws_its_ghost_and_caches_nothing`, `refusal_ghost_tests::the_ghost_retires_with_the_refusal` (ui lib: the ghost is freed, not only hidden).
- `refusal_ghost::tests::a_ghost_draws_dashed_in_the_dimmed_gouge_colour_and_never_in_a_path_colour`, `a_long_move_is_capped_in_dashes_not_in_length` (ui, path_lines-style structural asserts; no PNG).
- motion: `refusal_ghost::a_ladders_centre_cut_refusal_hands_back_the_moves_it_had_built`, `refusal_ghost::the_plunge_audit_hands_back_the_path_it_judged_beside_its_spot`, `machining2d::gen_error::tests::{a_ghosted_refusal_reads_exactly_like_the_refusal_without_it, the_ghost_rides_the_frame_and_the_sentence_rewrites_keep_it}`, `machining2d::ghost::tests::*` (cap, non-finite drop, frame map).

## How tested
`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` is green: motion suites ok (464 s, includes center_cut_law/owed/posed, entry_approach, ruling, finish3d, multiaxis, rotary_*, refusal_ghost), app suites ok (679 s, includes refusal_ghost, refusal_location, area_controls, center_cut_multiaxis, center_cut_owed, operations, scripting, mcp, posting, stock_sim_document), ui suites ok (112 s, lib includes refusal_focus_tests, refusal_ghost_tests, path_lines::tests, warned_moves). That is 3 steps, 21 min wall, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
- The on-screen look (dash length, dim level, how readable it is in the light theme) was not hand-checked. The GUI was not launched.
- No snapshot PNG changed, and no golden CL/NC changed: the change adds no output.

Changelog: A refused generation now draws the moves it had built before refusing as a dashed "ghost" in the refusal colour (display only; never cached, simulated or posted), and the script/MCP generate error names its move count (#261)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #261: with parts 1 (#349) and 2 (#678, #684) shipped, this covers the issue's whole ask: warned moves are marked, a refusal marks its spot, and a refused generation shows its partial path.

title: feat(cl,app): unwind continuous C at clear links against the machine's stated C travel
body:
Slice 2 of #33 (continuous C-axis live tooling). This covers item 2 of the 2026-11-08 owed list: unwinding C on links against a stated travel.

## What changed
- **`cl::unwind_c`** (new `crates/cl/src/cl/rotary_unwind.rs`) takes a path stamped by `stamp_c` and brings every stated C inside the machine's C travel by whole turns.
  - The path is split at its clear links. A clear link is a point the tool reached by a rapid that stands at the path's own clearance (the highest rapid Z, or the largest rapid radius), and only where that clearance is strictly beyond every point the tool cuts. On a standing bar's Rotary Contour, that is the point between each ring's retract and the next ring's plunge.
  - A stretch that fits the travel is left as stamped. A stretch that does not fit is moved by the fewest whole turns.
  - Each rewind is written into the path as the part-frame orbit it really is: rapid chords round the circle through the link point, each stating its C and the radial station pose, split so the machine's C-linear arc stays within the op tolerance. Verify, the solid bar audit, the steel laws and the post therefore all see the rewind. Nothing turns that a law has not judged.
  - Refused by name: a stretch whose own C span no whole-turn shift fits inside the travel ("... no clear link stands inside it to unwind at"), a travel that is not a range, a rewind that would need more than 100 000 chords, and a path carrying index-keyed records where an orbit would have to be inserted.
- **`rotary_gate::stamp_spindle_c`** now gets the machine inventory and runs `unwind_c` after `stamp_c` when the machine's rotary named C states a travel. This is the same axis that `machine::check`'s C letter gate (`c_letter_problem`) judges, so there is no second derivation. A machine that states no C travel keeps the stamped path byte for byte.
- `cl::rotary::{azimuth, ON_LINE}` are now `pub(super)` so the new module can share them.

Result: on a mill-turn stating C -360..360 (the shipped `millturn.mch`), a multi-ring Rotary Contour now generates, verifies and posts. Before this change the machine check refused it for C beyond the travel.

## Pinning tests
- `c_axis_unwind::a_rotary_contour_on_a_stated_c_travel_unwinds_at_its_links_and_posts`: the bar's rings wind past 720 deg when no travel is stated. With -360..360 stated, every C is inside the travel, the chain holds, C stays continuous, the rewinds are clearance rapids, they add no verify finding, and fanuc-lathe posts with no warnings.
- `c_axis_unwind::a_rewind_through_stock_is_convicted_by_the_verifier`: with the clearance plane left inside the box stock, the orbit chords are convicted as `RapidInStock`. This shows the verifier sees the rewind and does not assume it is clear.
- `c_axis_unwind::a_ring_wider_than_the_stated_travel_refuses_by_name`: with a travel of -90..90, generation refuses by name.
- `c_axis_unwind::two_rings_unwound_post_to_their_golden`: the golden below.
- `cl::rotary_unwind::tests::{three_rings_unwind_at_their_links_and_stay_a_chain, a_path_inside_its_travel_comes_back_unchanged, a_ring_wider_than_the_travel_refuses_by_name}`.

## Goldens
- **Added:** `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/c_axis_unwind.nc` (two rings at r 10, unwound at their link: `G01 X20 Z5 C-348.75 ... C0` orbit blocks at the link height).
- **Moved:** none. An unstated travel is a no-op, and existing fixtures state none.

## Gate
Gated on this branch after #848 merged (origin/main 2046357b merged in). The run used `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, which fell back to batch scope because a `cl` crate changed. Result: 9/9 steps green in 74 min (geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app incl. `c_axis_live`/`c_axis_unwind`/`rotary_letter`, ui from crates/ui, clippy -D warnings on all eight crates); logs in gate-logs/quick-20261111-145909. origin/main has since moved 35 commits (to 6458433f); they merge cleanly with this branch (`git merge-tree`) and were not re-gated. The pinning suites `c_axis_unwind` (4/4) and `cl` rotary (7/7) are green, as are `c_axis_live` and `rotary_letter` (run inside the gate). clippy -D warnings ran on the touched crates.

## Not exercised
- Rotary Parallel and Rotary Offset on a travel-limited C. They take the same `stamp_spindle_c` path and their radial retract cylinder counts as a clearance, but only Rotary Contour has an end-to-end test.
- Posting through `posting::` with the machine check (`check_document`) on an unwound op. The travel bound is asserted directly against the same bounds `c_letter_problem` reads.
- A real control. The orbit is written as G01 C blocks at the composite rapid feed, the same way the slice-1 post voices C rapids (owed item 5).

## Still owed on #33
1. A machine C-sense word.
3. Axial/face live-tool stations and G12.1 polar interpolation.
4. Arcs on a C turn.
5. Confirming the composite (degree-as-mm) rotary feed law on a real control.
6. live_tool words in a shipped machine.
- Possibly: a control roll-over word (modulo-360 C) as an alternative to orbit rewinds. See `docs/decisions/33-c-unwind.md`.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/33-c-unwind.md`.
No new user-facing command, so no MCP tool is owed.
Effort: high (not escalated).

Changelog: Continuous C-axis live tooling unwinds C at clear links against the machine's stated C travel. Each rewind is an orbit rapid that the verifier and the post see, and a cut wider than the travel is refused by name (#33)

Refs #33

title: feat(tools): draw a milling tool's cutter, neck and shank as a spun profile (#93 slice 2)
body:
Slice 2 of #93: a MILLING tool's own shape - cutter, neck and shank - drawn as a spun half-outline in the tool editor, the same way slice 1 (#475) did the holder. Lathe tools are untouched and keep their own editor (owner's ask on #93).

## What changed
- **Law (`camcraft-tools::cutter_profile`)**: `check(tool, points)` validates a drawn cutter against the tool's numbers and refuses by name: every spun-profile refusal (empty / too few points, negative or non-finite radius, open ends, runs back, ...), a turning tool, an outline that does not start at the tip, is not exactly the stated diameter within the flute length (never wider, never short), does not end at flute + shank length, is wider than the stated shank above the flute top, or folds back over itself. `parametric(tool)` is the outline the numbers draw. Slack 0.001 mm.
- **Stored data**: a new component `schema::ToolCutter` (reader/writer `app::tool_cutter`). It is **display only**: no generator, simulation or judging law reads it, so the numbers stay the truth. A drawn cutter moves no operation stamp (pinned).
- **Command**: `SetToolCutter::new(world, name, Some(points) | None)`, validated at creation, one undo step (undo restores the previous outline). `ChangeTool` refuses a number edit that would break a drawn cutter, by name ("reset the cutter profile to Parametric first"). `DeleteTool` / `DeleteEntity` snapshot it, so undo restores it.
- **MCP**: `get_tool_cutter_profile` and `set_tool_cutter_profile` (`crates/app/src/mcp/cutter_tools.rs`). Both go through the same `SetToolCutter`, so `undo`/`redo` work. Refusals use the law's own wording.
- **Project file**: additive `cutter` key on the tool record (`[z, r, arc]` per point). **No project-version step**: when the key is absent you get the outline the numbers draw, which is what every older file means. Save-load-save is byte-identical. A file whose drawn cutter disagrees with its tool is refused by name.
- **UI**: the Profile tab gains **Draw holder / Draw cutter**. The holder view stays the default and is unchanged. Draw cutter has Parametric (follows the numbers) / Custom (point table with arcs, insert/remove), the shared flat side view (the drawn cutter is filled when it validates and outlined in red when not, with the holder above it), a live refusal by name, a summary line (cutter Ø, flutes, overall), and **Apply cutter**, which queues one command. Parametric + Apply clears back to the numbers' outline. The holder view's side view now draws the landed drawn cutter. `side_view` and the points grid are shared between both views.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/93-spun-cutter-profile.md`.

## How tested
Gated **on this branch after #848 merged** (origin/main 2046357b merged in; the earlier local gate-tmp workaround was dropped and deleted, never pushed).
- `camcraft-tools` unit tests `cutter_profile::tests::*` (4): every catalog milling tool passes its own law; turning tools refused; refusals by name; a number edit re-judged.
- `crates/app/tests/tool_cutter_profile.rs` (5): `a_drawn_cutter_lands_undoes_and_moves_no_stamp`, `a_cutter_that_disagrees_with_the_numbers_is_refused_by_name`, `a_number_edit_that_breaks_the_drawn_cutter_is_refused_and_delete_restores_it`, `the_drawn_cutter_round_trips_and_older_files_load_without_one`, `the_cutter_is_drawn_and_undone_over_mcp`.
- `camcraft-ui` `egui_app::tests::tool_cutter` (4, AccessKit labels/state): the cutter view sits beside the holder, Parametric follows the numbers, Custom keeps edits, Apply cutter is one command and undo/redo walk it, a cutter that disagrees with the numbers is refused live and at Apply. Slice 1's `egui_app::tests::tool_profile` and `tool_holder` re-run green.
- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on head 943eee69: tools, 135 app suites (incl. tool_cutter_profile, tool_spun_profile, tool_body, holder_library, project_roundtrip, mcp*), 11 ui suites: all ok (14.5 min). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- A slice-1 UI test (`a_profile_refusal_retires_when_the_outline_validates`) first failed when the Draw holder / Draw cutter row sat above the holder view: the extra row pushed Apply profile out of view. The toggle now sits on the Body/Profile tab row, so the holder view keeps its height. The test was not changed.

## Not exercised
- The on-screen look of the side view was not hand-checked (no GUI launched). No snapshot PNG changed.
- Release tier and `--ignored` lanes were not run.

## Follow-ups
- #852 (P1, effort:high, area:sim): the simulation and the reach laws should read a drawn neck where it is narrower than the shank cylinder. Not wired here on purpose, and nothing in `tool_body::judged` / `stack` or any collision law is touched.
- Not mine, but noted: slice 1's drawn **holder** profile still has no MCP tool (#799 closed via #825, which shipped no MCP file).

## Still owed on #93
- Segment/parametric editing per stock tool kind beyond "numbers draw it" (for example editing the ball or chamfer by its parameters inside the outline editor).
- The issue's "preview snapshot" test (asserted structurally here instead, per the snapshot law).
- Feeding the profiles into the simulation and laws (#852; the issue lists it as out of scope).

Changelog: Tool editor: draw a milling tool's own cutter, neck and shank as a spun outline (Profile tab, Draw cutter), validated against its stated diameter and lengths, undoable, saved with the project, and settable over MCP (set_tool_cutter_profile / get_tool_cutter_profile) (#93)

Effort: high (not escalated)

Refs #93

title: feat(kernel): heal seam op and solidcore native-format importer corpus (M12.1 stage 3)
body:
Stage 3 of the M12.1 retirement gate. This adds a healing seam op and a solidcore-side importer corpus. No production path is switched to solidcore, and truck keeps its kernel role. This is partial work: `Refs #27`.

## What changed
- **`Kernel::heal`** joins the seam (`crates/kernel/src/lib.rs`).
  - solidcore runs the port's `api_heal_brep`.
  - truck returns `Unsupported { kernel: "truck", op: "heal" }`, because truck-modeling and truck-shapeops have no B-rep healing. The bench records that as not yet, never as agreement.
- **`crates/kernel/src/solidcore_import.rs`** (new): the heal impl, plus the port's native ASCII B-rep format (`.smb`): `write_smb`, `read_smb` (the raw reader, capped at 64 MiB) and `import_smb` (read, then heal, then the checks below).
  - The port's heal reports success whatever it finds, so the seam judges the result instead.
  - Before healing, it refuses an empty B-rep and a B-rep whose tolerance is not finite and > 0 (upstream HANG-24: the stitch never ends from tolerance 0).
  - After healing, the solid must pass the integrity check, be a closed manifold, have a positive finite measure, and keep its largest vertex-edge gap at or under `HEAL_GAP_LIMIT` = 1e-3 mm (a chosen bench limit, to revisit with real-world models). `vertex_gaps` is public so the bench can read the gap; it counts edges with no 3D curve as `unjudged_edges`.
  - `read_smb` refuses a file whose declared format version is newer than the port's (42), or whose declared zone tolerance is not finite.
  - `import_smb` returns `Imported { brep, notes }`. A zone tolerance the reader replaced or clamped becomes an `ImportNote::ZoneToleranceReplaced` diagnostic, and a model with any unjudged edge is refused.
- **Tests**:
  - `tests/heal_import.rs`: the heal and round-trip bench.
  - `tests/import_corpus.rs`: the corrupt-file corpus.
  - `tests/smb_util/mod.rs`: shared helpers. Every port call runs on its own thread under a 60 s bound, so a hang fails the test instead of stalling it.
- `docs/decisions/27-solidcore-healing.md`: decisions 1-6 (plus 5a, on allocation) and the findings.

## Readings (release)
**Heal, solidcore against closed form.** truck: Unsupported, pinned by `truck_offers_no_heal`.

| fixture | V solidcore | closed form | abs error |
|---|---|---|---|
| box 10 | 1000.000000000 | 1000 | 0 |
| cylinder r3 h10 | 282.743338815 | 90 pi | 8.5e-9 |
| box - through cylinder r3 | 717.256661205 | 1000 - 90 pi | 2.8e-8 |
| box \| box (L) | 750.000000000 | 750 | 0 |
| box, one edge round r2 | 991.415926583 | 1000 - 40 (1 - pi/4) | 4.7e-8 |

For every fixture the bbox deviation is 0.

**Native round trip** (write `.smb`, then import): the same five fixtures give the same numbers as above, all within 1e-6 relative.

**Vertex gap** (one vertex of the 10-box moved in the file):

| gap | healed vertex tolerance | import result |
|---|---|---|
| 1e-6 | 1e-5 (the zone tolerance) | V = 1000 exact |
| 1e-4 | grown to 1e-4 | V = 1000 exact |
| 5e-4 | grown to 5.4e-4 | V = 1000 exact |
| 2e-3 | - | refused (`InvalidResult heal`, "a vertex sits 2.000e-3 off its edges") |
| 1e-2 | - | refused (`InvalidResult heal`, "a vertex sits 1.000e-2 off its edges") |

- The port grows the vertex tolerance to cover the gap; it never moves the vertex back.
- For the accepted gaps, the tight bbox keeps the moved vertex: its deviation equals the gap.

**Corrupt corpus**: 22 files, every verdict pinned in `KNOWN_SMB_VERDICTS`. No panic and no hang anywhere.
- The importer refuses every corrupt file: blank, foreign text, binary noise, header only, a future format version, cut at 10/50/90 %, NaN or inf vertex, NaN zone tolerance, face count 2^32-1 or -1, a control-point count of 1e15, out-of-range surface or face index, a dropped face, and a 1.0 gap.
- Three edits leave the model whole: dropped final newline, zero zone tolerance, negative zone tolerance. These import as exactly the 10-box (volume and bounding box asserted). The two tolerance cases also carry the pinned note "zone tolerance 0e0 (or -1e0) replaced by 1e-4".
- Allocation: the port checks every declared count against the bytes left before it allocates, so with the 64 MiB input cap no file can force a large allocation (decision 5a).

## Findings against the port (pinned as not yet, not papered over)
- **The raw reader returns `Ok` with an EMPTY B-rep (0 faces)** for a blank file, plain text, binary noise, and a header with no body. The importer refuses these (heal's empty guard). The port did the same for a NaN zone tolerance, which the seam now refuses before the reader runs.
- **The raw reader returns `Ok` with a closed box whose vertex sits 1.0 off its edges**, and the port's heal accepts it by growing the tolerance. The importer refuses it with the gap limit.
- No upstream report has been filed yet; that stays on the list below.

## How tested
- Pinning tests:
  - `heal_keeps_every_fixture_at_its_closed_form`
  - `truck_offers_no_heal`
  - `native_round_trip_matches_closed_form`
  - `vertex_gap_is_closed_by_the_importer`
  - `corrupt_native_files_never_panic_or_hang`
  - `seam_refuses_degenerate_heal_and_oversized_files`
  - `heal_refuses_nonsense_brep_tolerance`
- `cargo test --release -p camcraft-kernel`: all suites green (agreement 2 + 2 ignored, blend 6, corrupt_input 6, heal_import 4, import_corpus 3).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: it planned only the kernel suites (debug) and passed, all 6 binaries green (12.0 min wall on the review-round head).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p camcraft-kernel`: passes.

## Not exercised
- The kernel heavy lane (`--ignored`): this PR adds or touches no ignored test, so it was not run.
- Third-party `.smb` files and the port's upstream corpus: not in-tree, so the corpus is built from the port's own writer output.
- Binary `.smb`: only ASCII is read and written.
- Gap healing on curved models: only a box vertex was moved.
- Edges with no 3D curve: counted as unjudged. `import_smb` refuses a model that has any; the seam's `heal` on an in-memory solid accepts them, because the port's own boolean results carry them (decision 3 records the risk).
- App, motion and ui lanes: the quick gate did not pick them (kernel-only diff). origin/main's motion build break (#844) was not touched.
- The production time bound: in tests every case runs on a thread with a 60 s timeout. The seam itself relies on the size cap and the tolerance guard plus the port's own `MAX_TOL_DOUBLINGS`; it cannot pre-empt a port call.

## Still owed before truck can be retired (updated)
1. The wasm CI job: `workflow_dispatch` only, which needs the maintainer's say on `.github`.
2. The first production consumer switched behind the bench (e.g. a boolean stock op), as its own reviewed PR.
3. Upstream reports to tangency-labs/solidcore for the pinned findings:
   - stage 1-2: `box & empty`, offset NaN, past-collapse offsets, WR-421 rim chamfer;
   - stage 3: the reader's `Ok`-empty on garbage, and heal growing tolerance over any gap.
4. A healing bench on imported real-world models with curved gaps. This needs a corpus we may vendor; STEP models go through truck-stepio first, with no solidcore STEP reader.
5. Then truck's kernel role is retired (STEP IO stays on truck).

## Review round 1 (reviewer comment on 6bd42c14)
1. Heal tolerance guard: now pinned by `heal_refuses_nonsense_brep_tolerance`. It calls `heal` directly at tolerance 0, -1, NaN and +inf, each under the 60 s bound, and asserts `InvalidInput { op: "heal" }`.
2. The open-sheet check can no longer skip: the sheet is asserted built and non-empty, then healed in the same kernel.
3. Intact files are asserted against the exact 10-box: volume and bounding box.
4. The zero and negative zone-tolerance cases now return a pinned `ImportNote` diagnostic. A future-version file is now refused rather than noted, because the reader would parse a newer layout with version-42 rules (decision 5). A NaN zone tolerance is refused by name before the reader runs.
5. `vertex_gaps` returns `VertexGaps { gap, max_vertex_tolerance, unjudged_edges }`, and its doc is fixed. The importer refuses any unjudged edge; in-memory heal accepts them, and decision 3 records why.
6. `HEAL_GAP_LIMIT`: the unit (mm) is stated at the constant, and it is called a chosen bench limit, to revisit with real-world models.
7. The provenance comment names where the `.smb` knowledge comes from: the port's writer output and its `BrepData::read_from_file` and `DATABASE_VERSION` rustdoc.
8. Allocations: the port does bound them (`checked_count` in `topology::brep_data`, `ensure_available` in the NURBS reads), recorded as decision 5a. A new corpus file with a control-point count of 1e15 is refused at once.

No new dependency. No `build.rs`, script or `.github` change.

Changelog: none (kernel bench and seam only; no production path uses it)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Refs #27

title: fix(motion): main compiles again - trochoid reads measure()/Stock after #783, seeds under the approach law
body:
**Main does not compile** (from 51979785, through 7f0928fe). Three PRs that each built alone collided once merged:

1. **#783 (motion onto Stock)** made `quality::measure` return `Result<PathQuality, StockError>`, and `stock_for` return a `Stock` instead of a `Dexel`. The trochoidal slot (#563/#778) still:
   - read `q.max_deg` and `q.max_at` on the bare result (`trochoid_slot.rs`);
   - passed the stock to `lifted_cut`, which took `&mut Dexel` (`trochoid_air.rs`).
2. **The #697 approach law** (`origin_approach::no_generator_seeds_the_clearance_plane_without_the_approach_law`) found the trochoid's `finish()` seeding with `PathBuilder::new` at X0 Y0 on the clearance plane.

**Changes:**
- **`trochoid_slot.rs`:** both `measure` calls go through one `gauge` closure that maps the stock error to a named `GenError` ("trochoidal slot: measuring stock: …", the wording the `stock()` closure already uses). The lifted-return read maps its error the same way. `finish()` seeds with `PathBuilder::approached`. Its first move is already a rapid, so the path is unchanged.
- **`trochoid_air.rs`:** `lifted_cut` takes `&mut Stock` and returns `Result<Option<Point3>, StockError>`. It cuts with `Stock::subtract_flat` (the same column-arm law as `Dexel::subtract`) and reads through `Columns::col`/`top_at`. A stock the reading can't serve is an error, never a pass.
- **`tests/trochoid_slot.rs`:** the two test call sites read the `Result`.

**How tested (Linux):**
- **The batch gate** on 2c05183c: geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, app (including the slow lane), ui and clippy all ok. Motion's one failure was `origin_approach` (item 2 above), fixed in 0f96b56b.
- **On 0f96b56b:**
  - the quick gate (motion suites 131 s, app) is green;
  - `origin_approach::no_generator_seeds_the_clearance_plane_without_the_approach_law` is green;
  - the `trochoid_slot` suite is green, including `trochoid_microlift_returns_land_on_air` (the lifted-return law still catches a return over uncut stock).

**Not exercised:** a GUI trochoid run. The law tests cover the behaviour.

title: feat(ui): the shell runs in a browser - eframe web runner, awaited GPU start-up (#31 rung 3)
body:
Rung 3 of #31 (M13.3), **retargeted to `main`; was stacked on #841** (it still contains #841's commits until that PR merges): the CamCraft shell now **runs in a browser**. This is a partial step (`Refs #31`): there is no file picker and no in-browser CI job yet.

## Review round (head `b6483d66`)

Fixes for the review of `1f903bd4`, as one plain commit on the same branch:

1. **Diagnostics reach the browser console.** New `crates/ui/src/diag.rs`: `diag_warn!` / `diag_info!` print to stderr / stdout natively, exactly as before, and call `console.warn` / `console.log` on wasm32, where std drops both streams. The stock eye's fall-back to the CPU march (`trace/eye.rs`), the file dialog's "cancelled" note and the other direct prints in browser-compiled UI code now go through it: 35 sites in 12 files. A law test fails on any direct print outside the seam, the native-only files and the tests. No new dependency: the console binding is eframe's re-exported web-sys.
2. **`poll_oneoff` does what its comment says.** It now succeeds at once, reports each clock subscription as elapsed (the caller's sleep is over) and writes the first skipped wait to the console with its length. A descriptor subscription gets an ENOTSUP event, also said in the console. It used to answer ENOSYS.
3. **The missing-imports message prints.** The import list is read with `|| true`, so an empty list reaches the named `die` instead of ending the script through pipefail.
4. **The wasm-bindgen install is announced and can be refused.** See the maintainer section below.
5. **The shim answers the nine imports and nothing else.** `fd_read`, the environ calls and the other unused exports are removed; the build already fails by name if the module asks for a tenth. Unknown clock ids answer EINVAL and a write, close or seek on a descriptor that is not open answers EBADF, each with one console warning. The two expected probe answers (ESPIPE for a seek on stdout, EBADF ending the preopen walk) are documented and not reported.
6. **The first browser target is clamped.** `view_pass::target_extent` now holds the pixel ratio to 0.1..=8 itself (1 for NaN), so no caller can size a zero or runaway target. The existing `target_extent_is_never_zero...` test covers zero, negative, huge, infinite and NaN ratios.

Re-proved after the fixes: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on head `b6483d66` fell back to batch: **all 9 steps ok, 0 failed (55.3 min)**, including the ui suites and `clippy -D warnings` on all eight crates. The gate ran on the branch as pushed; it still merges cleanly with `origin/main`, so no merge of main was taken.

`web/build-app-wasm.sh` exited 0 again (it installed the pinned CLI after printing what it would run). Headless Chrome, same rules as before, drew the first frame and opened the Stock page on a click. The stock-eye refusal now arrives as a console **warning**: `stock eye: the device binds no storage buffers to a fragment shader - the deviate sheet stands in`.

Not shown in the browser: the exact `eye.rs` line the review named ("the CPU march stands in"). On WebGL2 the composite refuses first, so the whole eye is refused and that line is never reached; it goes through the same macro as the line that did appear. `poll_oneoff` was not called during start-up either; the shim was checked in Node against a fake memory instead (16 checks, including the event layout and each console warning). The `CAMCRAFT_WASM_NO_INSTALL=1` refusal was not run.

Left open: camcraft-app's own diagnostics (its `tracing` events and direct prints) are still dropped in a browser - they need a console writer installed by the browser shell. Added to the owed list.

## What changed

- **Browser runner: `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell_web.rs` (new, wasm32 only).** An `eframe::App` over a `<canvas>` whose frame runs the same `shell::shell_layout` as the native window. The page starts it through one export, `camcraft_start(canvas_id)`. eframe's web runner was chosen over our own canvas glue because it was already in `Cargo.lock`, its web half needs no egui-winit, and it already does the DOM events, canvas sizing and awaited GPU start-up (about 4000 lines we would otherwise write and maintain). The reasoning is in `docs/decisions/31-wasm-web-runner.md`.
- **Shared 3D pass: `egui_app/view_pass.rs` (new).** The scene upload gate, target sizing, the View3D + traced-stock pass and the repaint law moved out of the native frame, unchanged, so the two shells cannot drift. `shell_window.rs` and `shell_window/frame.rs` now call it (frame.rs 409 -> 358 lines).
- **GPU waits that await.** `TracePass::new`, `Composite::new`, `StockEye::new` and `headless_gpu::device` each got an `*_async` twin holding the unchanged body with `.await` at the wait. The blocking forms are thin `pollster::block_on` wrappers, `cfg(not(wasm32))`, so native behaviour is unchanged. `pollster` is now a native-only dependency: a blocking wait in shared code no longer compiles for wasm32. The browser shell builds the stock eye on the event loop after its first frame and picks it up from a slot.
- **`trace/readback.rs` (new, native only).** `TracePass::trace` and `decode` moved there unchanged; `trace.rs` goes from 411 to 343 lines.
- **Native-only entries refuse by name on wasm32.** The `--headless` proof joins the windowed entry behind the same refusal; `shell::headless` is `cfg(not(wasm32))`.
- **Never a panic at start-up.** A missing canvas, a refused adapter or surface, or a runner without a device ends as text in `#camcraft-status` (`data-state="refused"`) plus a console error. The page turns uncaught errors and rejections into the same message.

## Dependency / script / workflow changes (needs-maintainer)

- `Cargo.toml` [workspace.dependencies]: `eframe = "=0.36.2"` (no default features; `wgpu`, `default_fonts`), `wasm-bindgen = "0.2.129"`, `wasm-bindgen-futures = "0.4"`. **No new crate enters the tree**: all three were already in `Cargo.lock` (eframe through egui_kittest, the others through wgpu). The lock diff is three lines, camcraft-ui's dependency list. All MIT OR Apache-2.0.
- `crates/ui/Cargo.toml`: those three as **wasm32-only** dependencies; `pollster` moved to the native-only table.
- `web/build-app-wasm.sh`: step 4 now links the UI as a cdylib (`cargo rustc -p camcraft-ui --lib --crate-type cdylib`, manifest unchanged) because an export does not survive the link of the binary. New step 5 runs the wasm-bindgen CLI whose version it reads from `Cargo.lock` (a matching one on PATH, else `cargo install wasm-bindgen-cli --version <lock version> --locked` from crates.io into `target/wasm-tools/bindgen`, never `~/.cargo`). **For the maintainer to decide:** that install downloads and builds the CLI and its dependencies, its build scripts run, and the CLI has no checksum in this repo. The script prints the exact command before running it, and `CAMCRAFT_WASM_NO_INSTALL=1` turns it into a refusal that names the version to put on PATH, copies the page and shim into `target/web/`, and fails if the module asks for a WASI import the shim does not export. **The `camcraft-ui` binary is no longer linked for wasm32** (#841 linked it); the cdylib replaces it.
- `web/index.html` (new): the page - canvas, status element, import map, module script.
- `web/wasi_shim.js` (new): answers exactly the nine `wasi_snapshot_preview1` imports the wasi libc under flecs asks for (clocks from the page, stdout/stderr to the console, a skipped wait for `poll_oneoff`, a named errno for the rest; `proc_exit` throws). Refusals and skipped waits are written to the console once each.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: **comment only** on the existing `wasm` job. Triggers unchanged (`workflow_dispatch` only). That job will now also install the wasm-bindgen CLI when it is run.

## How it was proved

- **In a browser (this machine, 2026-11-11).** `web/build-app-wasm.sh` exited 0 on the final tree and printed:
  - `linked .../debug/camcraft-cli.wasm`
  - `linked .../debug/camcraft_ui.wasm` (647 MB debug; 62 MB after wasm-bindgen)
  - `WASI imports answered by the shim: clock_time_get fd_close fd_fdstat_get fd_prestat_dir_name fd_prestat_get fd_seek fd_write poll_oneoff proc_exit`
  - `page ready in .../target/web`

  Chrome was then run headless only (`--headless=new --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader`, throwaway profile, a loopback static server on 127.0.0.1, driven over the DevTools protocol). Console and DOM read back:
  - `gpu: adapter "ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0 (SwiftShader Device ...)" via gl`
  - `camcraft-web: runner started`
  - `stock eye: the device binds no storage buffers to a fragment shader - the deviate sheet stands in`
  - `camcraft-web: first frame drawn (viewport target 600x400)`
  - status element: `data-state="running"`, document title `CamCraft - Untitled`, canvas 1264x705.

  A screenshot showed the whole shell: ribbon with icons, browser tree, viewport with the origin axes and view cube, properties pane, status line. A synthetic click on the ribbon's Stock door then opened the Stock page and selected Stock in the tree, so input, the command queue and the flecs world all work in the tab. The screenshot is kept out of the repo.

  One line was added to `web/index.html` after that run (an empty `rel="icon"` link, to stop the favicon 404); the page was not re-run for it.
- **Native gate:** `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/31-wasm-ui-shell` on head `1f903bd4` fell back to batch (Cargo change): **all 9 steps ok, 0 failed (35.3 min)** - geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app and ui (cwd crates/ui) suites, and `clippy -D warnings` on all eight crates.
- **Pinning tests (native):** `diag::tests::shared_ui_code_prints_only_through_the_diag_seam`, `diag::tests::the_macros_take_println_shaped_arguments`, `view_pass::tests::target_extent_is_never_zero_and_scales_with_the_pixel_ratio`, `view_pass::tests::a_browser_frame_with_no_egui_timer_still_follows_the_document`. The moved `shell_window::redraw_tests` still run against the moved `redraw_delay`. The existing GPU suites run the blocking wrappers over the new async bodies.

## Not exercised

- **WebGPU.** Headless Chrome offered no WebGPU adapter here, with or without the software-adapter flags, so wgpu ran on WebGL2. The awaited stock eye was refused by name *before* its await, so an error scope actually awaited in a browser has not been seen. The `*_async` bodies are exercised natively through their blocking wrappers only.
- **Refusal paths in the browser** (no adapter at all, missing canvas, `proc_exit`): written, not triggered.
- **Anything past the first frame and one click**: importing a model, generating a toolpath, simulation, posting, keyboard and text input, resizing. Opening and saving cannot work yet (`file_dialog` answers "cancelled" on wasm32).
- **Thread sites.** No code changed: every spawn already goes through `thread::Builder::spawn` and handles the error (import runs inline; playback and the CPU eye refuse by name), and generation goes through rayon. None of this was run in the browser.
- **A release build** of the page, and the `wasm` CI job itself.
- The native GUI was not launched (by rule).

## Still owed on #31

1. An async file picker behind `file_dialog`, so a model can be opened and a program saved.
2. An inline playback path where the worker cannot spawn (today it refuses by name), and a browser check of generate/import.
3. The in-browser CI job (manual trigger), and the Pages deployment (#688).
4. A WebGPU run, to see the awaited stock eye land.
5. `lib.rs` still allows dead code on wasm32: 17 native-only helpers (gpu_select, the backend mask, `world::seed`, the recent-files read) have no caller there and need gating one by one.
6. A console writer for camcraft-app's `tracing` events and direct prints, which a browser still drops.
7. `shell.rs` is still 923 lines (only an import and a `cfg` changed here); the viewport panel is the seam to split.

Changelog: CamCraft's shell runs in a browser: eframe web runner over a canvas, awaited GPU start-up, page and WASI shim built by web/build-app-wasm.sh (file picker and CI job still owed) (#31, PR #847)

Refs #31

title: fix(sim): judge a tool body by the band stack the simulation draws
body:
Retargeted to `main`; was stacked on #837. `origin/main` merged in (ed8616b4; conflict in `operation/mod.rs` resolved by keeping both `body_judged` and `fixture_route`). Today's main (fixture routing #489, holder libraries, plasma/swing laws) adds no new `Cutter` literal or cylinder reader: `fixture_route` sweeps `verify::steel_stack` (already the band stack), `posting_index_swing` reads the total length (equal for both shapes).

## What changed
A tool with a modelled body (#368 mesh, #93 drawn spun holder) is now judged by **one** shape: the band stack the fixture laws sweep and the simulation draws (`tool_body::stack`), not the single cylinder enclosing it (option 1, decided by the orchestrating session; `docs/decisions/835-reach-reads-band-stack.md`).

- `sim::verify::BodyBands` (new, `body_bands.rs`): the body's bands above the shank, fixed capacity (33) so `Cutter` stays `Copy`. Refused back to the cylinder (`None`) when the stack is the plain holder cylinder (no body, no change), non-finite, starts in the flutes, reaches past the enclosing holder/shank, or tops out elsewhere. `Cutter::judged` re-checks it against the geometry the laws read.
- `Cutter::body` + `Cutter::with_body` / `holder_bands`: `atoms()` emits the body's bands in place of the holder band.
- `reach.rs`: law (c) and (c3) read `Cutter::judged(cx.tool, cx.cutter).holder_bands()`. Law (c) convicts a move once per group (shank, then holder-or-bands), worst offender first - a no-body tool's output is identical (one band per group).
- `operation::generate`: one cutter `Cutter::of(&tool).with_body(&geom, &holder)` feeds both `VerifyContext.cutter` sites, `contain_into` and `rotary_into`.

## Which laws moved / kept
- **Moved to the band stack:** (c) shank/holder reach, (c3) mid-turn sweep, (b2) solid law, the containment kinds' solid law, posed rapids (via the judged cutter), the rotary field law. Fixture laws (c2/d2, mesh) already read it. (e) cycle reach reads the total length, which is equal for both shapes.
- **Kept the enclosing cylinder, named:** drill-reach axial holder and cross-drill holder refusals, cross-drill `part_clear`, probe stylus reach. A refusal naming the holder of a tool with a body gains "the tool body is judged here by the cylinder enclosing it, Ø... mm to ... mm above the tip" (`operation::body_judged::name_enclosure`, applied in `run_job`); a probe path with a body carries the same words as a note. Moving them: **#842** (filed).
- **Unchanged, not shape verdicts:** magazine fit (widest diameter is the right reading), 5-axis shank-avoid dodge (generator choice), posed-contact (f2) shank excuse.


## Review round 2 (head f74f878d)
- **Contiguity is checked** (finding 2): `BodyBands::of` returns `None` (the enclosing cylinder stands) for a stack that is not contiguous from the shank's top - a gap, a late first band, or an overlap. Pinned: `tool_body_bands::a_gapped_stack_is_refused_and_the_cylinder_stands`, `a_late_starting_stack_is_refused_and_the_cylinder_stands`.
- **Raised foot, direction stated** (finding 3): when a body's foot stands above the shank's top, the gap is judged at the **shank's radius** (the shank carried up, as the fixture laws have since #368), where the cylinder judged it at the enclosing holder's. That is **looser where the body is wider than the shank, stricter where the shank is wider**. Both sides pinned: `tool_body_bands::a_raised_foot_over_a_slim_shank_is_judged_looser_than_the_cylinder` (cylinder: ShankHit, bands: clean; body in the wall still ShankHit), `a_raised_foot_over_a_fat_shank_is_judged_stricter_than_the_cylinder` (holder group now convicts too). Kept on the shank radius because nothing modelled is wider there: the body's envelope starts at its own lowest vertex, and with a body the record's holder is replaced by the body - the only steel in the gap is the shank (reasoning in the decisions file).
- **(c3) behind (c)** (review note): a stock-only `ShankHit` used to stand down the mid-turn sweep on that move and could hide a swing through the PART (both block the post, but the user was told "uncut stock"). Now (c3) is skipped only where (c) already named the part; on a stock-only conviction it runs and a part `SweepHit` is reported (a stock sweep there is dropped as the same event). Applies to tools without a body too (can only add a part warning). Pinned: `tool_body_bands::a_swing_through_the_part_is_not_hidden_behind_a_stock_shank_hit` (fails on the old code: only `ShankHit{part:false}`).
- **Gated on the merged tree** (f74f878d, `--base origin/main`): quick gate sim/motion/app/ui all ok (45.7 min); app `verify`, `tool_spun_profile`, `tool_body_view` ok; clippy -D warnings on sim, app, motion clean.

## Readings, stepped body (Ø8 end mill; r6 nose 14..34 above tip, r20 flange 34..49; enclosing cylinder r20 from 14 to 49)
| case | before (cylinder) | after (bands) |
|---|---|---|
| wall 10 mm off axis, tip 30 deep (flange 4 mm above stock top) | `ShankHit{at:1, part:true}` | none |
| wall 10 mm off, tip 40 deep (flange 6 mm into wall) | ShankHit | ShankHit (still) |
| wall 5 mm off, tip 30 deep (nose in wall) | ShankHit | ShankHit (still, once) |

## Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/tool_body_judged.rs`)
- `the_band_stack_is_never_smaller_than_an_imported_mesh_body` - samples a faceted, turned, lifted mesh (nose, cone, flange, taper): envelope, swept stack and the reach laws' stack all >= the body's radius at every sample.
- `the_band_stack_is_never_smaller_than_a_drawn_profile_with_cones_and_arcs` - same against the drawn outline (line, cone, convex arc, concave arc) sampled on its true circles.
- `a_stepped_nose_clear_of_the_wall_is_no_longer_warned`, `a_band_that_reaches_the_wall_is_still_warned`, `a_tool_with_no_body_reads_unchanged`
- `a_stack_that_is_not_this_tools_is_refused_and_the_cylinder_stands`
- `the_simulation_draws_the_stack_the_reach_laws_judge` - `sim_tool_body::for_operation` holder bands == judged cutter's bands == fixture stack.
- `a_law_that_keeps_the_cylinder_names_it`
- plus the five round-2 tests in `crates/app/tests/tool_body_bands.rs` (above)

## How tested
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/743-sim-revolved-tool-body`: motion, app (incl. tool_body_judged, probe_reach, rotary_verify, solid_law, drill_reach, ...), ui green; sim step failed to compile on first run (two sim test `Cutter` literals missed `body: None`), fixed and the same sim suite list re-run green (16 binaries).
- By name: app `verify`, `tool_spun_profile`, `sim_tool_body`, `tool_body`, `tool_body_view`, `tool_body_judged` green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Goldens moved
None. No golden, snapshot or existing assertion changed; test edits are only `body: None` in `Cutter` literals (motion `solid_law`, sim `midmove_pose`, `overhang_laws`).

## Not exercised
- Release tier / `--ignored` heavy lanes (incl. sim/app envelope lanes) not run.
- A leaning (posed) body through (c)/(c3) is not pinned on its own (same per-band code path).
- No end-to-end generated op with a body against a part wall (pinned at the verify level plus the world-level drawn==judged check); posed/leaning bodies through (c)/(c3) and the rotary law with a body not separately pinned (same per-band code paths).
- GUI not launched.

Changelog: A tool body (imported or drawn) is judged by the same band stack the simulation draws by the reach, sweep, solid and rotary laws - a stepped holder whose flange stands clear is no longer warned; laws that still use the enclosing cylinder say so; a mid-turn swing through the part is no longer hidden behind a stock shank warning on the same move (#835)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #835

title: feat(ui): camcraft-ui builds and links for wasm32 (#31 rung 2)
body:
Rung 2 of #31 (M13.3): `camcraft-ui` now builds **and links** for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`. `web/build-app-wasm.sh` produces `camcraft-ui.wasm` next to rung 1's `camcraft-cli.wasm`. This is a partial step (`Refs #31`). The UI does not run in a browser yet.

## What changed

- **Shell split (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/`).** `shell.rs` was 1676 lines. It is split three ways:
  - `shell_window.rs` (native-only, 381 lines): the winit event loop, `Shell` struct, window and surface, GPU bring-up, native refusal dialog and the redraw timing helpers.
  - `shell_window/frame.rs` (native-only, 409 lines): the per-frame draw and the winit `ApplicationHandler`.
  - `shell.rs` (923 lines, every target): what any shell shares - `shell_layout`, the dock tabs, the viewport panel, the sim readouts and the headless proof.

  The moved code is unchanged apart from imports and visibility. `VIEW3D_FORMAT` and `Tab::title` became `pub(crate)`. `gpu_init`, `frame_watch` and `os_quit` are also `cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))`. On wasm32, `egui_app::run` refuses the windowed entry by name (exit 2) rather than pretending.
- **`crates/ui/src/file_dialog.rs` (new).** All 13 `rfd::FileDialog` sites (`state.rs`, `state_per_op.rs`, `state_setup_post_options.rs`, `state_tool_library.rs`) now go through one `FileDialog` seam with the same builder API. Native builds forward to rfd unchanged. On wasm32 the seam answers `None` (cancelled) and prints a stderr line naming #31.
- **`crates/app/src/clock.rs` (new).** `camcraft_app::clock::Instant` is `std::time::Instant` natively and `web_time::Instant` on wasm32, where std's `Instant::now()` panics. It is used at app's 6 timing sites and ui's `state.rs` / `frame_watch.rs`. In geometry, `slice.rs` now reads the clock only while projection profiling is switched on (an environment variable, which a browser can never set), so no new dependency is needed there.
- **`crates/ui/src/lib.rs`.** `#![cfg_attr(target_arch = "wasm32", allow(dead_code))]`. Nothing calls the shared shell on wasm32 until the web runner lands, which would otherwise give 543 dead-code warnings. Native builds keep the lint.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/31-wasm-ui-shell.md`.

## Dependency / script / workflow changes (needs-maintainer)

- `Cargo.toml` [workspace.dependencies]: `web-time = "1.1"`. **No new crate enters the tree.** web-time 1.1.0 was already in `Cargo.lock` through winit/egui. The lock diff is one line (camcraft-app's dependency list). License MIT OR Apache-2.0, pure Rust.
- `crates/app/Cargo.toml`: `web-time` added as a **wasm32-only** target dependency. Native builds do not compile it for app.
- `crates/ui/Cargo.toml`: `egui-winit` and `rfd` moved to `[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]`. Native builds are unchanged; wasm32 drops them (egui-winit 0.36.2 does not compile there).
- `web/build-app-wasm.sh`: a new step 4 builds and links `camcraft-ui.wasm` with the same flecs patch and checks that the file exists.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: **comment only** on the existing `wasm` job, which runs the script. Triggers are unchanged (`workflow_dispatch` only).

## How it was proved

- **wasm32, recorded local run** (Windows, Git Bash, clang 21 from msys2, wasi-sysroot 34): `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<worktree>/target bash web/build-app-wasm.sh` exited 0 and printed:
  - `build-app-wasm: linked .../wasm32-unknown-unknown/debug/camcraft-cli.wasm` (rung 1, still links)
  - `build-app-wasm: linked .../wasm32-unknown-unknown/debug/camcraft-ui.wasm` (rung 2, about 576 MB debug, the whole UI crate incl. egui, egui_dock, egui-wgpu/wgpu, viewport and app)

  No camcraft-ui warnings on wasm32. The tracked `Cargo.lock` was restored afterwards.
- **Native:** `cargo check -p camcraft-ui --all-targets` is clean. The quick gate was `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, which fell back to batch because of the Cargo and geometry changes. Results: **all 9 steps ok, 0 failed (37.2 min)** - geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app, ui (cwd crates/ui) suites and `clippy -D warnings` on all eight crates.
- **Pinning tests (native):**
  - `file_dialog::tests::file_dialog_builder_keeps_every_setting`: the seam keeps title, filters, directory and file name.
  - `clock::tests::clock_seam_is_monotonic_and_does_duration_math`: the alias does the Duration maths `logging::elapsed_ms` and the play worker rely on.
  - The existing `redraw_tests` moved with their code to `shell_window` and still run. The `#[test]` count is unchanged apart from the two new tests.

## Not exercised

- **No in-browser run.** I have no browser here. `camcraft-ui.wasm` links, but it has not been instantiated, and on wasm32 its entry only refuses the windowed path. Running it needs the pieces still owed below.
- The wasm32 halves of `file_dialog` (returns None) and `clock` (web_time) are type-checked and linked, not executed.
- The native GUI was not launched (by rule). The windowed code moved verbatim and is covered by compile, clippy and the ui suites.

## Still owed on #31

1. A browser runner: eframe's web runner or the egui web glue, calling `shell::shell_layout`. Remove the wasm32 `allow(dead_code)` when it lands.
2. Async GPU bring-up in place of the `pollster::block_on` sites (`egui_app/gpu.rs`, `trace.rs`, `trace/composite.rs`, `headless_gpu.rs`).
3. An async file picker (rfd `AsyncFileDialog` or `<input type=file>`) behind `file_dialog`, with a pending-result slot in `State`.
4. Run-inline fallbacks where `std::thread::spawn` is used (generate, job, stock_play_worker, state, cpu_eye).
5. The JS shim for the wasi imports, wasm-bindgen CLI 0.2.129, the page, and the in-browser CI job.
6. `shell.rs` is still 923 lines, down from 1676. The viewport panel (about 460 lines) is the next seam to split out.

Changelog: camcraft-ui now builds and links for wasm32 (browser shell still owed): native window split from the shared shell, file-dialog and clock seams (#31, PR #841)

title: feat(post): Synthetos TinyG post processor (3-axis mill)
body:
Stacked on #715 (grblHAL post): this branch is #715's head plus one commit, and extends the same registry and test lists. Fork synced at v0.16.0 (through #715's base).

## What changed

A new built-in post, **TinyG** (`assets/posts/tinyg.cps`, 3-axis mill), for Synthetos TinyG controllers, and a generic machine, **TinyG 3-axis** (`assets/machines/tinyg-3axis.mch`). The post is specced from TinyG's public wiki (Gcode Support, Homing and Limits, Flow Control and Footers, Inch and Millimeter Units Mode) and the LinuxCNC G-code reference TinyG states it follows (behaviour only; the firmware source is GPL and was not read), structured after `grblhal.cps`. Decisions in `docs/decisions/836-tinyg-post.md`.

- Header `G21|G20 G17 G90 G91.1 G94 G64`: the words M30 does not reset on TinyG (units, arc-centre mode and path-control mode persist). No `%`, O word, N numbers, G40 or G80; no tool length word (as #710 decided for grblHAL: the measured length belongs to the operator or sender).
- **No canned cycles**: a CYCLE record writes nothing and the hole's expanded chain posts as plain moves, with the dwell as `G4 P<seconds>` after the move that reaches the bottom; a dwell whose chain never reaches it is refused, not dropped. Tapping is refused by name.
- **Tool change**: the Z lift, then `T<n> M6` alone on its line, then `M0` on the next - TinyG's M6 only records the tool, so the stop is the operator's change; the first tool gets it too. Tools T1-T31; a larger number is refused by name. Because of that M0 the after-operation stops are pinned in `tinyg_post.rs` rather than through `after_op.rs`'s mill list (whose tests count every M0 as the operator's stop); the home refusal is in that list.
- **Z lift as grblHAL's** (#715): `G53 G0 Z<safe_retract>` only when the machine file states it, else `G0 Z<clearance>` in the work offset, refused by name when unknown or not above the stock. No G28/G30. The generic machine states no `safe_retract`.
- **Comments** drop `!` (feed hold), `~` (cycle start), `%` (queue flush), `/`, `{`, `$` and the comment delimiters; a note opening with `msg` is led by "- " so TinyG does not echo it as a message. Lines are kept to 191 content bytes (248 usable receive bytes, 192-byte RTS window) and a longer one is refused by name.
- Lengths at four decimals in either unit (TinyG checks an arc's start and end radius against its centre). Extension `.gcode`.
- Refused by name: control/wear compensation (G41/G42 are rejected by the board), going home, tilted moves; probing is refused by the engine (no probe hooks: no parameters or expressions on TinyG).

## How tested

- `conformance`: TinyG in POSTS, REFUSED (`tap_plate`, "tapping"), EXTENSIONS; the synth stream drops only the tap. Goldens in `golden/nc/tinyg/` (12) and `golden/nc/synth_tinyg.nc`.
- New `tinyg_post.rs` (11 tests): registry and library; every word letter and G/M code of the posted programs is in TinyG's table; lift, lone `T M6`, `M0`, spindle after; drilling as plain moves with `G4 P1.5`, owed dwell refused; tap refused once; T32 refused, T31 posts; homed machine lifts with G53; unknown or buried lift refused; after-operation M0/M1 counted apart from the tool-change stops, home refused; hostile names; inch output.
- Cross-post lists extended: `comment_escape`, `control_comp`, `wear_comp`, `post/tests/comp`, `fanuc_post` (non-RTCP), `inverted_post`, `coolant`, `coolant_followups`, `after_op` (home refusal), `machine` (library expectations).
- **Firmware replay:** every golden and the synth golden replayed through the edge-next firmware's own parser (`tests/host/input_harness.py`) and through its parser + canonical machine + arc generator + planner (`tests/host/corpus_replay.py`, build 450.03, commit d4014951): 13 files, 749 lines, 1626 planner blocks, 0 refused lines, 0 alarms, 0 numeric findings.
- Gate: all 211 `camcraft-app` test binaries except `lathe_thread_travel` green on the final tree (`--test-threads=6`), `camcraft-post` `comp` 9/9, `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test tinyg_post -- -D warnings` clean. `scripts/gate.sh quick` stops on `lathe_thread_travel.rs:83` (missing field `hand`), the pre-existing break on this branch's base that #712 fixed on main; not touched here.

## Not exercised

**Not yet run on a TinyG board** - the author maintains the edge-next firmware and will dry-run a posted program on a v8 board next (no stock, Z raised, hand on feed hold) and report on #836. The Setup pane's End-units row still appears only for Tormach, although the script reads `EndUnits`. No spindle-up dwell after M3 is written (TinyG suggests `G4 P2` where needed); a post option for it is recorded as a follow-up in the decision file.

Changelog: Synthetos TinyG post processor (3-axis mill) and a generic TinyG 3-axis machine; drilling posts as plain moves with G4 dwells, M0 after each tool change, tapping, G41/G42, probing and go-home refused by name

Fixes #836
