title: feat(wcs): anchor the WCS on a picked circle's centre; tidy the WCS page
body:
## What changed

**Shared pick primitive** - `crates/app/src/pick/circle.rs` (next to the #692 pick graph): `circle_centre(world, &GeoSel)`, `circle_of_edge(graph, edge)`, `circle_of_run(features, run)` return a `Circle { centre, axis, radius, closed }` or a named `CircleRefusal` (`Straight`, `TooShort`, `NotCircular`, `NotAnEdge`, `Gone`). The edge pick resolves to its **run** (one straight stretch or one arc), so an arc of a filleted rim works too. The fit reuses `feature_arc::fit_arc` and its tolerances, and checks every vertex. A non-circular edge is refused, never guessed. The axis sign is canonical, so a hole in a top face reads +Z. The centre is in the active setup's view frame (#326), the frame the WCS is set in.

**Command + MCP** - `SetWcsAtCircleCentre` (`crates/app/src/commands/wcs_circle.rs`) resolves the circle when the command is created and wraps `SetWcsOrigin` at the centre: one undo step, and undo restores the previous origin. The MCP tool `set_wcs_circle_centre { edge: {model, id}, rotation? }` (`crates/app/src/mcp/wcs_circle.rs`) runs the same command and returns the circle's centre, axis and diameter. The camcraft-mcp skill doc lists the tool. No MCP follow-up is needed.

**WCS page** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page.rs`, split out of the 1894-line `pages.rs`):
- Three collapsible sections: *Origin and orientation*, *Quarter turns* and *Anchor on*.
- The six value fields sit in a two-column grid, label and field on one row, with the fields in one column.
- The quarter turns are two rows of three equal buttons ([X+ Y+ Z+] / [X- Y- Z-]), plus *Level* and *Set Origin* as two equal halves. Every row spans the pane's width.
- The anchor grid is a 3x3 compass of equal cells (up to 72 x 30), placed exactly and centred.
- *Anchor on* has a third choice, **Circle centre**. It shows a "Pick a circular edge" toggle and then the result, e.g. "Circle Ø 20.00 mm, centre (0.00, 0.00, 10.00)", or "Not anchored: <reason>". While the toggle is armed, a viewport click takes feature edges only, one run per click, and hover highlights what a click would take. A landed pick disarms the toggle. Choosing Circle centre disarms the box markers, and the other way round.
- The Bottom/Middle/Top radios are now a plain "Z level" row. Beside the 120 px label column they widened the section past a narrow pane.

**Plumbing** - `CommandKind::SetWcsCircle`, and a new `state_wcs.rs` that also takes over the existing `SetWcs` arm (`state.rs` shrinks). The viewport routes clicks through `wcs_pick.rs` (anchor markers + circle pick), which shortens `interact.rs`. `feature_click::ask` returns the circle ask while armed.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/circle_centre.rs` (new, 5 tests) uses a plate with a drilled 8 mm hole (32 chords), off-centre at (5, -3):
  - `a_drilled_hole_rim_gives_its_true_centre_axis_and_radius`: centre within 1e-6, Ø 8, axis +Z, through a real ray pick, and again with the part moved.
  - `a_straight_edge_is_refused_by_name`.
  - `an_elliptical_rim_and_a_face_are_refused_never_guessed`: ellipse gives `NotCircular`, face gives `NotAnEdge`, stale id gives `Gone`.
  - `the_anchor_command_places_the_origin_and_undo_restores_the_previous_one`: undo, redo, and a refusal never builds a command.
  - `mcp_set_wcs_circle_centre_anchors_on_a_rim_and_refuses_a_straight_edge`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page_tests.rs` (structural, no pixels):
  - `the_page_has_three_sections_and_one_row_fields_in_one_column`
  - `quarter_turns_are_equal_buttons_filling_the_pane`
  - `the_anchor_points_are_a_centred_compass_of_equal_cells`
  - It also holds the three `turn_wcs` tests, moved verbatim from `pages.rs`. The test count is unchanged.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_circle_tests.rs`:
  - `a_rim_click_anchors_the_origin_on_its_centre_and_undo_restores_it`: combo, then the pick button, then a viewport click on a boss rim, then G54 at the centre. The page states the circle, and Undo restores (1, 2, 3).
  - `a_face_is_refused_by_name_and_lands_nothing`
- Gate (macOS, worktree target):
  - Ran green: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `camcraft-app --lib`, the full `camcraft-ui` lib and integration suites (459 lib tests), and these app suites: circle_centre, feature_pick, feature_pick_wire, mcp, mcp_setup, mcp_pick, mcp_live, one_wcs, setup_wcs, commands_undo, wcs_align, wcs_view_pose, face_origin, vertex_pick, pick.
  - Not run: `cargo xtask gate quick` itself. Its dry run fell back to every crate, which is batch-sized.

## Not exercised

- Nobody has looked at the page in the real app (hand check below). No snapshot PNG changed. The release-lane `egui_shell_snapshot` was not run; the WCS page is not in that frame.
- A circle on a rotated or aligned setup is covered by the view-pose transform, and the app test covers a translated part. No rotated-setup test was added.

## Hand check

1. Open the WCS node and check the three sections. Each field should sit on one row with its label. Narrow the properties pane: the turn buttons should stretch evenly, and the compass should stay centred with equal cells.
2. Set *Anchor on: Circle centre*, then press *Pick a circular edge*. Hovering a hole rim or boss edge should highlight it. A click should move the WCS origin to the circle centre at the rim's height and show "Circle Ø … , centre (…)". Ctrl+Z should restore the previous origin.
3. With the pick armed, click a straight edge: the status line and the page should say it is straight, and the origin should stay put.
4. Switch back to Stock box: the compass and "Pick markers in viewport" should work as before.

Changelog: WCS page: anchor the origin on the centre of a picked circular edge (hole rim or boss), undoable and with MCP tool `set_wcs_circle_centre`; page laid out in sections with one-row fields, even quarter-turn buttons and a 3x3 anchor compass

- `assets/posts/carvera.cps` reads the `Smoothing` / `SmoothingMode` PARAMs (#616). The 28-tool starter catalog moves from a Rust table in `tools.rs` to `assets/tools/catalog.json`, a `camcraft-tools/1` library (the #300 envelope), embedded with `include_str!` like the posts. `catalog()` keeps its signature, names, order and values, so no call site or test changes. `camcraft-tools` reads it with a small strict reader (`catalog_asset.rs`: format/version/units/name/duplicate/unknown-key/`is_sane` checks, errors name the tool); a failing embedded asset is logged and yields an empty catalog, never a panic. title: feat(post): grblHAL post processor (3-axis mill)
body:
Fork synced at v0.16.0.

## What changed

A new built-in post, **grblHAL** (`assets/posts/grblhal.cps`, 3-axis mill), and a generic machine, **grblHAL 3-axis** (`assets/machines/grblhal-3axis.mch`). The post is specced from the G-code list in grblHAL's public core README and the LinuxCNC G-code reference (behaviour only; grblHAL's GPL source was not read), structured after `tormach.cps`.

- Header `G21|G20 G17 G90 G91.1 G94 G40 G80`; no `%`, O word, N numbers or G64.
- **No tool length word** (no G43 / G43.1 / G49): on grblHAL the offset belongs to the controller's tool-change handling, and a G49 would discard a measured length. This departs from the issue's G43.1 default; reasoning in `docs/decisions/710-grblhal-post.md`.
- `G53 G0 Z<safe>` then `T<n> M6` **alone on its line**; no G28/G30.
- Canned cycles G73/G81/G82/G83/G86/G89 with G98, dwell P in seconds.
- Refused by name: control/wear compensation (G41/G42), tapping (G84), going home after an operation (G28/G30 positions are controller settings), tilted moves, and probing (the engine refuses it, since the post has no probe hooks).
- **Z lift without trusting an unhomed machine Z0.** With `$22=0` grblHAL takes its power-on position as machine zero, so `G53 G0 Z0` could rapid down. `G53 G0 Z<safe>` is written only when the machine file states `safe_retract` (= "it homes"). Otherwise the lift is `G0 Z<h>` in the work offset, where h is the section's `ClearancePlane` or a higher Z already commanded; it is refused by name when h is unknown or not above `StockZTop`. The generic machine states no `safe_retract`.

## How tested

- `conformance`: grblHAL in POSTS / REFUSED (`tap_plate`, "tapping") / EXTENSIONS. Goldens in `golden/nc/grblhal/` (12) and `golden/nc/synth_grblhal.nc`. The synth stream drops only the tap.
- New `grblhal_post.rs` (9 tests): registry and library, grbl program shape with no length/G64/G28/G30/G84 word, Z lift before a lone `T M6`, dwell P1.5 for 1500 ms, one named tap refusal, inch output, a homed machine lifting with G53, the work-offset lift without homing (clearance, a higher commanded Z, origin shift), and the named refusal of an unknown or buried lift height.
- Cross-post lists extended: `comment_escape`, `control_comp`, `wear_comp`, `post/tests/comp`, `fanuc_post` (non-RTCP; the tilt refusal is now looked for among all warnings, since grblHAL also refuses its lift on that bare stream), `inverted_post`, `after_op` (stops plus the home refusal), `coolant`, `coolant_followups`, `machine` (library expectations).

Quick gate (debug) on the final tree: 28 camcraft-app binaries, among them conformance 6 (goldens unchanged by the lift fix, their machine states safeRetractZ 0), grblhal_post 9, fanuc_post 11, after_op 10, coolant 7, machine 32 and posting 17, all green; camcraft-post `comp` 9/9; camcraft-ui lib `machines_pane` 6/6 and `post` 19/19; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib -- -D warnings` clean. Whole-crate `clippy --tests` stops on the pre-existing `lathe_thread_travel.rs:83` compile error (missing field `hand`), which is on upstream main and not touched here.

## Review fix (smoothing, head 6129a904)

With per-operation smoothing (#616) on, the post writes one `(SMOOTHING NOT WRITTEN - GRBLHAL STATES NO SMOOTHING TOLERANCE)` note per program (grblHAL lists G61 only, no tolerance word) and resets the ask per section. Pinned by `smoothing::fanuc_and_mazak_name_the_ask_once_and_write_no_unbounded_word` (now covers grblHAL). Goldens unchanged (smoothing off).

## Not exercised

**Not yet run on a real grblHAL controller or its simulator - testers welcome.** Anyone with a grblHAL machine: please post a program with this post, dry-run it (no stock, Z raised, hand on feed hold), and report on #710, especially the Z lift before each tool change and at the end. The Setup pane's End-units row still appears only for Tormach, although the script reads `EndUnits`.

Changelog: grblHAL post processor (3-axis mill) and a generic grblHAL 3-axis machine; G41/G42, G84, probing and go-home are refused by name; a smoothing ask is named once, never written unbounded

Fixes #710

title: feat(app,ui): set the WCS from any set of feature picks (#701)
body:
You can select edges, vertices, faces and cylinder walls and say which axis each one sets (#701) - the WCS lands on the fitted frame, undoable like any other placement.

## The change

**App lane** - `pick::roles.rs`: `Role` (`Origin | X | Y | Z`) and `align_roles(world, picks) -> Result<Alignment, String>`, returning the same `Alignment` `pick::align`'s 3-2-1 fit already returns, so one fit law answers both. Frame law: among the axis picks present, read in the priority order Z, X, Y - first exact, second projected perpendicular, third derived to close the right-handed frame (a third axis pick is overridden wholesale, not blended). An origin pick anchors on the feature's natural centre; without one the origin stays the model's own. Refusals come back as words, in order: too few picks, a duplicated role, fewer than two axes, an unresolvable datum, an unsupportable tilt, a stale feature id. Cylinder walls fit by covariance null-space (Jacobi) plus a Kasa circle, on the wall's local facets transformed by the feature's `setup_align::view_pose` - the same law the plane fit already uses.

**UI lane** - the Setups page grows a "Set WCS from features" row (`egui_app::wcs_pick_row.rs`) over a draft module (`wcs_pick.rs`): arming it keeps the toolbar's pick mode (faces, edges, corners and walls all feed the one draft), the role box says what the next pick sets, and each viewport pick is stamped into that role's slot - re-picking a role replaces its pick in place. One draft at a time: arming this row disarms the plane-pick and axis-pick drafts and vice versa, and the wcs draft pauses while its setup row is hidden (the #664 law). Apply is gated live by `align_roles` itself - the refusal words ride the row inline and on the disabled button, so the UI's why is the command's own words - and queues the existing undoable `CommandKind::SetWcs`; the same command the WCS pane's anchor grid already sends. No new command kind, no world writes outside commands. Rationale in `docs/decisions/701-wcs-from-features.md`.

## Pins (red before the fix, green with it)

- `wcs_roles::z_face_x_edge_and_origin_corner_reproduce_the_3_2_1_frame` - a Z face, X edge and origin corner digit-for-digit reproduce `align_321`.
- `wcs_roles::the_third_axis_role_is_derived_right_handed_never_read` - three axis picks: the third is overridden wholesale and the frame is right-handed.
- `wcs_roles::the_origin_projects_onto_a_z_face_and_anchors_on_its_centroid` - an origin vertex pick anchors on the face's centroid, projected onto its plane.
- `wcs_roles::a_tilted_bore_wall_fits_its_real_axis_and_centre` / `a_bore_wall_picked_as_z_stands_upright_with_a_pinned_sign` - the wall fit, both flat and tilted, sign pinned by the axis role.
- `wcs_roles::every_degenerate_role_set_is_refused_by_name` - each refusal sentence, pinned.
- `egui_app::wcs_pick_tests::*` - four kittest tests on the live row: arming keeps the pick mode and stops the other drafts; an incomplete set greys Apply and shows the app's own words; role picks land in the draft (never in the open operation) and Apply queues one undoable `SetWcs` that undo/redo round-trips; re-picking replaces only that role's pick.
- `wcs_pick::tests::*` - three draft-module tests: role default and mutual disarm, replace-in-place, a paused draft takes nothing.

## Tested

title: feat(post): a PathPilot plasma post for the Tormach 1300PL
body:
**Stacked on #676** (#670, plasma profile), which is stacked on #674 (#669, plasma kind). Review only this PR's own commit, `2645a023`.

A **PathPilot plasma post for the Tormach 1300PL** (#671). Every word below was checked against UM10720 v1223A ([UM]) or Tormach's PathPilot Post Processor Guidelines, Plasma column ([PG]).

| Word | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `G20`/`G21` | units | [PG] |
| `G90 G91.1 G94 G17 G40 G49 G80` | modal reset, once | [PG]; [UM] §6.2.2 |
| `G64 P0.005 Q0.005` | path blending (P in inches even under G21) | [UM] §6.2.1 p.50; [PG] |
| `G54` | work offset | [UM] §6.2.1 |
| `G43 H1` | torch length offset | [PG] ("always H1"); [UM] §6.2.2 |
| `G30` | go to the G30 height | [UM] §6.2.1-6.2.2 |
| `G0 X Y` | rapid to the pierce point, never Z | [UM] §6.2.1 |
| `M200` | AutoFS (feed, THC volts, pierce height and delay, amps) | [UM] §6.3 p.51, §7.2 p.54 |
| `M207`/`M208`/`M209 P` | pierce height / cut height / pierce delay, only when the op states them | [UM] §6.3.1 p.52, §7.2 |
| `G15` | ohmic probe; WCS Z = 0 | [UM] §7.1 p.54 |
| `G16` | rise to pierce height, fire, delay, go to cut height, THC on | [UM] §7.1; [PG] |
| `G1/G2/G3 X Y [I J] [F]` | the cut, XY only | [PG] |
| `G41.1`/`G42.1 D<kerf>` … `G40` | control compensation, each on its own line before a straight lead | [PG] |
| `M205` | torch off, Z to the G30 height | [UM] §7.2 |
| `M30` | end | [PG] |

- **Never written:** S, M3-M9, M6, G95-G99, canned cycles.
- **M6 conflict:** [PG] says M6 is unsupported on plasma, but [UM]'s test program writes `T1 M6`. This follows the issue and [PG]; the conflict is recorded.

## What changed
- **Script:** `assets/posts/tormach-plasma.cps`, registered as "Tormach PathPilot Plasma", the only `PLASMA_POSTS` entry. Milling posts decline a plasma stream, because they lack the torch hooks.
- **Stream:** #676's records are carried into the post stream: `PLASMA …`, `TORCH ON C<id> …` and `TORCH OFF C<id>` (the `.cl` v5 records without `; `).
  - The parser reads both spellings; malformed records are refused by line number.
  - New properties: `PlasmaKerf`, `PlasmaCompensation`, `PierceHeight`, `CutHeight`, `PierceDelay` (absent = AutoFS), `PlasmaFeed`, `PlasmaReversed`, `Contour`, `ContourRole`, `ParentContour`, `SmallHole`.
  - New hooks: `onPlasma`, `onTorchOn`, `onTorchOff`.
  - `machine.kind` is now a script property.
- **Engine torch law** (`cnc_torch.rs`), refused by name:
  - a TORCH with no header, a second header;
  - ON while lit, a wrong or extra OFF, a rapid while lit;
  - a section or stream left lit;
  - a script without both torch hooks.
- **Post refusals:**
  - a non-plasma op, a Plasma Profile path with no plasma record;
  - rpm, coolant (other than off), a rotary or tilted move;
  - Z on a lit move, a canned cycle, a dark feed;
  - comp under a computer offset, wear comp;
  - a machine that isn't `kind: plasma`.
- **AutoFS:** under AUTOFEED, no F is written. A small hole then runs at the AutoFS feed, with an operator comment; refusing it would block every default plate with a hole.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/671-plasma-post.md` (the sources and ten choices). CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md and assets/posts/AGENTS.md are updated.

## Golden (`tormach-plasma/plasma_plate_with_holes.nc`, inch; excerpt)
```
G20
G90 G91.1 G94 G17 G40 G49 G80
G64 P0.005 Q0.005
(T1 PLASMA TORCH - KERF 0.0591)
G54
G43 H1
G30
(C0 INNER IN C4 - SMALL HOLE 65% FEED)
G0 X3.3465 Y0.7874
M200
M207 P0.1496
M209 P0.5
G15
G16
G1 X3.3465 Y0.9547 F63.98
...
M205
G30
```
Siblings: `_mm.nc` and `_control.nc` (`G41.1 D0.0591` … `G40`). The CLI post is byte-identical to the inch golden.

## How tested
- **`plasma_post` (5):**
  - the inch and mm goldens, with structural checks: no Z/S/T/M3-M9/M6, per-contour order, G30 after every M205, ending `G30 M30`;
  - the in-app dump equals the `.cl` golden;
  - the control-comp golden;
  - a stream round-trip, plus malformed-record refusals;
  - an in-app 1300PL document posts through the gate.
- **`plasma_post_refusals` (5):** every refusal, the engine torch law, every milling builtin declining the stream, and the registry.
- **Pins updated:** plasma_machine, machine_library, plasma_profile, golden_cl and conformance.
- **Gate:**
  - those suites plus posting, camcraft-post and camcraft-cl;
  - also tormach_post, control_comp, coolant, after_op, program_comments, fanuc_post, lathe_post, per_op_files and probe_guard;
  - clippy is clean.

## Not exercised (why this is a draft): a PathPilot Hub 1300PL simulator run
It should check:
1. G20 and G21 both load and run, and `G64 P0.005 Q0.005` reads as inches under G21.
2. `G43 H1` without `T1 M6` is accepted.
3. Whether a bare `G30` after `M205` also travels XY (a time cost only).
4. `M207`/`M209` after `M200` override AutoFS.
5. G1 moves with no F take the AutoFS feed.
6. `G41.1 D…` on its own line, a straight lead, then `G40`, with the offset on the right side.
7. G2/G3 under G91.1.
8. Probe and pierce at each G0 point, THC on, M205, and the part matches.

title: feat(post): Doosan DNM + Fanuc post processor (#614)
body:
(fork synced at v0.16.0)

Implements a dedicated post-processor dialect for Doosan DNM vertical machining centers with Fanuc 0i / 31i-M controls (#614).

## What changed

- **`assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`**:
  - Clean-room implementation specced from published Fanuc 0i-MODEL F operator programming manuals, Renishaw MP700 / Inspection Plus manuals, DN Solutions Operation Manual `MV0009OPE241_v0`, and real Doosan DNM machine sample program from Issue #614.
  - **High-Speed Smoothing / AICC (`G5.1 Q1 Rx` / `G5.1 Q0`):** Modal Fanuc AI Contour Control lookahead smoothing with machining condition selection (levels `R1` to `R10`, default `R5` matching the real Doosan DNM sample program). Automatically deactivated (`G5.1 Q0`) prior to canned drilling cycles (`G73`, `G81-G89`), probing, tool change, and program close. Out-of-range smoothing levels are strictly refused by name.
    * *Citation:* FANUC Series 0i-MODEL F Operator's Manual (B-64604EN-2/01) §3.3 (p. 19/33, p. 20/34), §3.3.2 (p. 22/36), §14.1 (p. 377–386). Requires Fanuc AICC I (A02B-0340-S603) or AICC II (A02B-0340-S605).
  - **Renishaw Inspection Plus Probing (`G65 P9832` / `G65 P9833`):** Emits `G65 P9832` (probe optical turn-on) on its own block before protected positioning moves (`G65 P9810`) and surface measurement (`G65 P9811`), and emits `G65 P9833` (probe optical turn-off / sleep) on its own block at the end of the probing sequence before spindle stop/retract. Unknown probing styles are strictly refused by name.
    * *Citation:* Renishaw MP700 Probe System Installation and User's Guide (H-2000-5142-02-A) Chapter 4 (p. 4-2 to 4-17) and Chapter 5.
  - **Rotary Table Brake (4th-axis A on separate blocks, no name sniffing):** Emits `M11` (unclamp) on its own separate block before rotary positioning, and `M10` (clamp) on its own separate block after positioning before cutting (never inline with motion blocks). Continuous 4th-axis contouring unclamps before motion and restores clamping at section end. Strict refusal by name if undeclared via options/properties (`rotaryClamp`/`rotaryUnclamp` or `rotaryBrake`) or machine definition.
    * *Citation:* DN Solutions Operation Manual `MV0009OPE241_v0` Part 5 §3 (p. 180) and Part 8 §3 (p. 232) Alarm 2323.
  - **Chip Conveyor Codes & Strict Refusal:** Requires codes to be declared via post options (`chipConveyorStart` / `chipConveyorStop`), properties, or machine definition, and strictly refuses undeclared codes by name.
    * *Citation:* DN Solutions Operation Manual `MV0009OPE241_v0` Part 5 §3 (p. 180) and Part 5 §2.13 (p. 137).
  - **Through-Spindle Coolant (TSC) & Strict Refusal:** Emits Doosan high-pressure TSC M-code `M88` (with `M89`/`M09` on shut-off) when declared in the machine coolants table, or `M8` when `useM8ForTSC` is enabled. Strictly refuses undeclared through-tool coolant by name if the machine lacks a through-tool entry.
    * *Citation:* DN Solutions Operation Manual `MV0009OPE241_v0` Part 5 §3 (p. 180) and Part 6 §2.6 (p. 217).
  - **Manifest cleanup:** Removed unverified `axisInversion` and `probeAxisInversion` manifest flags pending mirrored-stream equivalence test goldens.
- **`docs/evidence/614-dnm5700-sample.nc`**:
  - In-tree real-world sample G-code program provided by community user `@spikeypineapple` on Issue #614 comment 6764944619 confirming real-world DNM 5700 syntax for `G5.1 Q1 R5`, `M07`, and Renishaw Inspection Plus macros.
- **`assets/machines/doosan-dnm.mch`**:
  - Registered in `posting::MACHINES` and `crates/app/tests/machine.rs` as `"Doosan DNM 5700"` (Kind: Mill).
  - Updated with official DN Solutions DNM 4500/5700/6700 Specification Catalog numbers (X/Y/Z: 1020/570/510 mm, rapids: 36/36/30 m/min, cutting feed: 15 m/min, spindle: 40-12000 RPM, 18.5 kW, rigid tapping, 30-tool ATC, coolants M8/M7/M88, 4th-axis rotary table A).
- **Decision Record**:
  - Recorded in `docs/decisions/614-doosan-dnm-post.md` with all manual citations, page numbers, and design choices.

## How tested

- **`crates/app/tests/doosan_dnm_post.rs`** (7/7 passing):
  - `doosan_dnm_posts_basic_milling_clean`: basic program structure, preamble, tool change, work offset, retracts, safe end.
  - `doosan_dnm_through_spindle_coolant_modes`: verifies M88/M89 default TSC and M8 option.
  - `doosan_dnm_rotary_brake_clamp_unclamp`: verifies separate block emission (`M11`, motion block, `M10`) around A-axis moves with `rotaryBrake: true`.
  - `doosan_dnm_high_speed_smoothing_aicc`: verifies `G5.1 Q1 R5` engagement, `G5.1 Q0` deactivation before canned drilling cycles, and custom level `G5.1 Q1 R8`.
  - `doosan_dnm_chip_conveyor`: verifies M31 start and M33 stop with explicit configuration.
  - `doosan_dnm_probing_modes`: verifies `G65 P9832` (probe on) before moves and `G65 P9833` (probe off) at end.
  - `doosan_dnm_refuses_undeclared_codes_by_name`: verifies strict refusal by name for undeclared TSC, undeclared rotary clamp (tested on both generic VMC and DNM machine to ensure no name sniffing), unknown probing style, unbounded smoothing level, and undeclared chip conveyor codes.
- **`crates/app/tests/machine_library.rs`** (11/11 passing):
  - `every_machine_file_in_assets_is_in_the_library`: verifies Doosan DNM 5700 machine is mounted and registered.
- **`crates/app/tests/machine.rs`** (33/33 passing):
  - `every_shipped_machine_mounts_and_speaks_its_declaration`: pinned Doosan DNM 5700.
- **`crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`** (6/6 passing):
  - `every_builtin_posts_every_golden_byte_exact` across all goldens.
  - `every_builtin_registry_entry_compiles`, `every_builtin_declares_its_controls_file_extension`, `the_dialects_actually_differ`.
- Clippy `-D warnings` is completely clean.

Changelog: Doosan DNM post processor aligned with real machine sample program and manual citations (G5.1 Q1 R<n> smoothing, Inspection Plus G65 P9832/P9833 probe on/off, separate block M10/M11 rotary clamp, and strict refusal of undeclared codes) (#614)

Fixes #614

title: feat(ui): viewport origin gizmos wear their names (#727)
body:
With several setups on screen, every origin triad looks alike - nothing in the viewport says whose zero is whose (#727).

## The change

Every origin gizmo now labels itself at its origin. Each work-offset triad draws the entity name the Setup pane already uses (`G54` for the first setup, `Setup2/WCS` for the second) in bright triad blue at the ordinary overlay-label size; the dimmed world axes draw `World` in neutral gray dimmed by `WORLD_DIM`, like the lines under them. `Gizmo` (`interact.rs`) grows one `name` field, filled in `gizmos()` - which already honors the Models pane's eye (`hidden_offsets`) and the `show_world_axes` gate, so a hidden offset loses its name with its lines for free. `overlay_labels` places each name just below the projected origin (`NAME_DROP_UV = 0.02`, same currency as `axis_note::NOTE_DROP_UV`), emitted before the gizmo's `X`/`Y`/`Z` tips. Only the letters keep the big `is_axis_label` font. Rationale in `docs/decisions/727-viewport-gizmo-labels.md`.

## The switch (#645)

On top of the names, the review on #645 asked for a user switch, so the browser pane grows a `Show origin names` checkbox next to `Show world origin axes`. It gates only the name rows: the big `X`/`Y`/`Z` letters and the triad's strokes ignore it. The choice is a per-user preference, not document state - nothing touches the world or the command history - and it persists in `view.json` in the OS config folder next to the recents file (`recent`'s resolver, #662, so `CAMCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR` overrides the folder), written at once on the flip and read back at startup. The default is ON, the #727 decision: shipping the switch changes no existing viewport. A missing, unreadable or corrupt file - or a foreign one, the `camcraft-view/1` format tag says - starts at the defaults with a logged reason, never a crash, and unknown keys stay ignored so newer builds keep working.

## Pins (red on main, green with the fix)

- `gizmo_tests::the_dimmed_world_axes_are_labelled_world` - the fresh world's set carries `World`, neutral gray (equal channels) and dimmed like the axes.
- `gizmo_tests::each_triad_is_labelled_with_its_own_offset_name` - two setups: both `G54` and `Setup2/WCS` label their own origins, bright against the letters.
- `gizmo_tests::an_offset_name_stands_at_its_origin_not_its_axis_tips` - the name rides the projected origin horizontally, a small uv drop below it, not crowded onto the tips.
- `gizmo_tests::a_hidden_work_offset_drops_its_name_with_its_gizmo` - the pane's eye and the label agree.
- `gizmo_tests::gizmo_names_are_not_the_big_axis_letters` - `is_axis_label` still answers only X/Y/Z.
- Re-pins: label counts 3→4 (fresh world), 6→8 (two gizmos), 3→4 (moved origin); `axis_note_tests`' fresh-world set pins exactly `["World", "X", "Y", "Z"]`, which fixes each gizmo's emission order name-first.
- `setup_chip_tests`' no-G54-on-Setup2's-op clause narrows to plane chips (`" · "`): the `G54` origin name is Setup1's own, legitimately - the law was about op chips, and it still holds there.
- `structural::origin_names_paint_on_and_quiet_off_letters_and_lines_always` - the re-review's both-states shell check: with the switch on the seeded document's `G54` name row paints inside the viewport (the properties pane also reads `G54`, so the probe sits between the pane anchors, as the view-cube check does); the checkbox click drops it from the painted frame while the `X`/`Y`/`Z` letters and the triad's strokes come through untouched. The test redirects `view_store` to a temp folder so the flip never writes the real user's `view.json`.
- `crates/app/tests/view_prefs.rs` (new integration suite) - the persistence law: a flipped choice round-trips through the file across a "restart", a missing file is a quiet default start, a corrupt or foreign-format file starts at the defaults with a reason and never crashes, unknown keys stay ignored, and a `CAMCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR` override is the folder the choice round-trips through (`recent::config_dir_for` with a fake getter, as `recent_files` does).

## Tested

- Red first: with only the pins committed, `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- gizmo_tests axis_note_tests` ran 8 failed / 7 passed, exactly the new and re-pinned label tests - e.g. the fresh world's labels were `["X", "Y", "Z"]` with no name.
- Green: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- gizmo_tests axis_note_tests setup_chip_tests` - 17 passed, 0 failed.
- Full lib: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` - 490 passed, 0 failed (5 ignored). An earlier run of the same command failed only on `structural::shell_structure_light`, a theme-sync test this change never touches; it passes in isolation and on re-run - pre-existing parallel global-theme-state flakiness, already noted on #638.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test view_prefs` - 5 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` - clean.
- Not exercised: the on-screen labels themselves - the producers are pinned instead.

Changelog: viewport origin gizmos now wear their names - each work-offset triad shows its Setup-pane name at its origin, the neutral world axes show World (#727) - and a persisted "Show origin names" checkbox in the browser pane turns the name rows on and off, kept in the per-user `view.json` (#645)

Fixes #727

title: feat(tools): align a vendor STEP by ISO 13399 tool coordinate systems
body:
Second slice of #370 (and part of #361): auto-aligning a vendor STEP by its ISO 13399 tool coordinate systems.

## What changed
- `ToolCsysReport::align_tool_body()` extracts the tool axis and tip offset (`-dot(origin, axis)`) strictly from CIP (coordinate system in process, ISO 13399-303 §3.3) so that the cutting reference point sits at Z = 0 in the tool frame, pointing up into the spindle along +Z. No fallback to CSIF is performed since CSIF denotes the mounting interface, not the cutting point; missing, ambiguous, or degenerate CIP refuses by name.
- `ToolBodySpec::from_step_auto(&path)` reads both mesh facets and coordinate systems from a vendor STEP file, aligning it with zero manual offsets. Stated non-mm length units (e.g. inches, cm) are normalized consistently across both geometry and coordinate systems via `step_units::mm_per_unit`.
- `SetToolBody::from_step_auto(&world, tool_name, &path)` attaches the auto-aligned tool body as one undoable command.
- `tool_body_view::load_aligned(&path)` returns `LoadedBody` carrying the auto-alignment result or fallback reason, preserving `load` backwards compatibility.
- In the tool editor (`ToolBodyUi`), importing a STEP file with ISO 13399 coordinate systems automatically sets the axis and tip offset with the note "aligned by ISO 13399 coordinate systems"; importing a file without them or with degenerate/ambiguous coordinate systems falls back to default numeric placement ([0, 0, 1] axis, 0 offset) with a note naming why.
- Manually editing the axis combo or tip offset in the UI clears the alignment note to avoid displaying stale provenance.
- Test fixture `testdata/models/tool_csys_box_iso13399.step` combining a B-rep box and ISO 13399 placements.
- `docs/decisions/370-tool-csys-align.md`.

Merged `upstream/main` and clean.

## Readings
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test tool_csys`: 11/11 pass.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test tool_body`: 12/12 pass.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib tool_body`: 12/12 pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Pinning tests
- `iso_13399_tool_csys_aligns_automatically`
- `a_file_without_tool_csys_falls_back_by_name`
- `degenerate_tool_csys_falls_back_by_name`
- `cip_degenerate_with_csif_valid_must_refuse`
- `origins_and_facets_in_non_mm_units`
- `step_with_tool_coordinate_systems_aligns_automatically`
- `step_without_tool_coordinate_systems_falls_back_by_name`
- `step_with_degenerate_coordinate_systems_falls_back_by_name`
- `tool_body_view_load_aligned_handles_step_csys_and_fallback`
- `import_tool_body_from_step_auto_aligns_in_editor`
- `import_tool_body_from_step_without_csys_falls_back_by_name_in_editor`
- `manual_axis_edit_clears_align_note`
- `pick_tip_sets_manual_placement_note`

Changelog: Tool bodies: align a vendor STEP by its ISO 13399 tool coordinate systems (#370)

title: fix(post): an explicit M5 after a probe's tool change in every post
body:
Was stacked on #579 (#570, probe search limit and feed-only approach), which merged on 2026-11-10; this PR now holds only #574's change against main.

## What changed
Every mill post now writes an explicit spindle stop between a probe's tool change and length offset and its first move. Today the probe is safe on a Tormach only because PathPilot's `M6` stops the spindle, which is a property of the control, not something the program says.
- **Rule:** in `startPreamble`, `probeStop = spindleWait && !(sRpm > 0)`. Only a probe states 0 rpm, because tools refuse 0. After the spindle block and before coolant, the post writes the stop.
- **Per post:**
  - Fanuc, Haas, Tormach, Sinumerik, Heidenhain: `M5`.
  - Mazak: `MOTOFF`, its own stop word.
  - Fanuc Lathe: untouched (no probing).
- **Unchanged:** cutting sections and older streams post byte-identical output.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/574-probe-m5.md`.

**Stack merge (`fd1076af`):** #579 branched from a main older than #174's protected probe moves, so merging it hit conflicts in three Fanuc goldens and broke `probe_guard`. The merge commit resolves both.
- #579's new feed from the safe plane down to the approach plane now posts as a protected move: `G31` plus the `#5063` alarm on Fanuc, `G38.3` plus the `#5070` check on Tormach.
- `probe_guard` expects one more protected move per mode.
- `fanuc/probe_corner.nc` and `tormach/probe_guard_moves.nc` are regenerated to match.

#579 will need the same resolution when it takes main.

**Golden diffs from #574 itself:** each file gains one `M5` line right after the `G43` line:
- `fanuc/probe_bore_centre.nc`
- `fanuc/probe_corner.nc`
- `fanuc/probe_corner_negative.nc`
- `fanuc/probe_edge_negative_x.nc`
- `tormach/probe_guard_moves.nc`

Until #526 merges, some posts still write a probe's spindle start (`S0 M3`) before the new stop. The flag is computed separately, so it works in either merge order; Heidenhain will have a small hand-merge next to #526's lines.

title: feat(motion,app): Trochoidal slot - engagement-controlled trochoid operation (#220 slice 1)
body:
Slice 1 of #220: an engagement-controlled trochoid generator and a standalone **Trochoidal slot** operation. Branched from upstream/main; the fork is synced at v0.15.0.

## What changed
**The generator** (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/trochoid_slot.rs`, `trochoid_loops.rs`, `trochoid_air.rs`), specced from Otkur & Lazoglu 2007 and Rauch, Duc & Hascoet 2009.
- **Loop shape:** each loop is the front arc of a circle of radius ρ = B / cos 10°, with B = (W − D)/2 by default. The arc runs wall to wall and meets each wall at 10°.
  - On a straight chain the loops are shifted copies, so they never cross. Classic full-circle trochoids always cross the previous loop, and the verifier holds the post on a same-depth crossing.
  - A wall move between arcs cleans the cusp, and a fillet (the smoothing radius) blends it into each arc.
- **Start and end:** a helical bore of radius B at the start. A stepped fan of arcs closes the far end.
- **Returns:** microlift (default 0.3 mm, retracing the arc just cut at the return feed) or retract.
- **Engagement:** measured with the Adaptive pins' dexel yardstick (`quality::measure`) on each candidate level. The planner tries steps from 100% of the user's step down to 7%, and a note says when the step was cut. Adaptive's planner raster was not reused because it counts finished walls as contact (see the decision file).
- **Lifted returns over air:** a new `machining2d::lifted_cut` checks each lifted return against the in-process stock.
- **Refused by name:**
  - a channel narrower than the tool (it suggests a plain Slot);
  - a loop wider than the room;
  - a limit no step can hold (the message gives the lowest reading, where it was, and at which step);
  - a loop leaving the channel;
  - a crossing (the verifier's own `crossed_pairs`);
  - a lifted return over stock.

**The operation:** `OpType::TrochoidalSlot` (kind 39) in the ribbon's 2D mill family.
- **Authoring:** two endpoints and a width, like Slot, verified against the slot's stadium.
- **Parameters:** loop width (auto), forward step, max engagement, return, microlift height, smoothing radius, stock to leave, heights, stepdown, cutting/return/plunge feeds, climb.
- **Undo and editing:** create and edit are undoable (`CreateOperation` / `EditOperationParams`). It has a small Geometry/Heights/Passes/Feeds page.
- **Project file:** a `trochoidal_slot` params entry. There is no `PROJECT_VERSION` bump, following the probe op's precedent (#108/#344) for an appended kind. Older builds won't read a document that uses the new kind.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/220-trochoidal-slot.md`.

## How tested
- **motion `trochoid_slot`** (7 tests, plus 2 unit tests):
  - A full-width slot (D10 in W16, 1 mm step) measures θmax **66.5°**; a straight Slot in the same channel measures **180°**.
  - A 60° limit forces the step down, and the note says so.
  - The verifier is clean (no crossing, gouge or rapid-in-stock) for climb and conventional, microlift and retract.
  - Microlift returns land on air, and the check catches one placed over stock.
  - Named refusals; the loops post as arcs.
- **app `trochoid_op`:** create and edit undo/redo; generate verifies clean and posts G03; a too-narrow channel is refused by name; project round trip.
- **New goldens:** `golden/trochoid_slot_small.cl` and `golden/nc/trochoid_slot_small.nc` (Fanuc, G02/G03).
- **Edited tests:** `ribbon` and `probe_op` pinned the probe as the last kind; they now pin index 38, and kind 39 is pinned.
- **Passing:**
  - motion `adaptive_band`;
  - app mill2d_b/c, ribbon, tool_law, probe_op, golden_cl, fanuc_post, project_roundtrip, operations, commands_undo, conformance, heidenhain_block_form, slot_caps, drill_prior_kinds, pick_doors, setup_align, wall_column_gouge, drilling_axial;
  - ui kind/ribbon/tab tests (including `every_registry_kind_gets_its_tab_bar`) and ui `operations`;
  - clippy on motion, app and ui (`-D warnings`).
- **Runtime:** the `trochoid_slot` binary takes about 80 s in debug when run in parallel. Each test is under 25 s alone.

## Not exercised (draft)
- **No run yet:** a GUI hands-on check, and a Hub or machine run of the posted arcs. This adds new posted G-code.
- **Deferred to later slices:** Adaptive's trochoidal mode (Done means 2), the corner-overload pin, centre-line picking from a model chain (typed endpoints today), the in-plane cutting return, feed reduction where engagement rises, and wall finishing when the loop band is narrower than the room.

Changelog: Trochoidal slot operation: an engagement-controlled trochoid along a typed centre line - measured contact angle held under a limit by adapting the step, microlift or retract returns, named refusals (#220, slice 1)

Refs #220

title: feat(ui): detect pockets and slots on the Model page and create their operations
body:
Was stacked on #512 (pocket and slot recognition), which merged on 2026-11-10; this PR now holds only its own two commits against main.

## What changed

The Model page gains a **Pockets and slots** section (#511):
- **Detect pockets / slots** runs `app::recognize::pockets_of` once per click.
- Each recognised feature is a row: kind, slot width/length/ends, floor Z, depth, tightest corner, islands.
- Each row has a **Create Pocket / Create Slot** button. It queues one `CreateOperation`, selects the new op and opens its page, as one undo step. The button's tooltip names the tool it will use (the last document tool that fits the kind, the ribbon's quick-add rule). With no tool it is disabled.
- The scan is view state keyed by model and document version. Any document change hides the list, and Create refuses ("detect pockets again"), so no row offers coordinates the part no longer has.

The planning (name, seed, tool-sized helix, feature mapping) moved into `app::recognize::plan_operation`, with the shared seed in `operation::seed_params`. The MCP `detect_pockets {create}` tool calls the same code, so a click and an agent create the same operation. `ui` holds no recognition logic (layering ui → app).

## How tested

- New `pockets_tests` (ui lib), 4/4:
  - `detect_lists_the_slot_and_the_pocket`: a part with a through slot and a closed pocket lists both, with the right row text.
  - `create_adds_each_operation_as_one_undo_step`: the slot becomes a Slot cutting into the stock and the pocket a Pocket on the part's floor face, each opens its page, and one Undo removes each.
  - `a_changed_document_makes_the_list_stale`
  - `a_model_without_geometry_is_refused_by_name`
- `scripts/gate.sh quick`, escalated to batch, 812 s: geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion and app all green. This includes `mcp`, `mcp_pockets`, `pocket_recognition`, `operations` and `project_roundtrip`, so the moved seed is behaviour-identical.

body:
﻿Answers the docs lane of #291 with two pieces, per the plan discussed there.

**`examples/`** - a complete `first-part.camproj` the guide can teach on: our own clean-room flange fixture (model embedded as facets, so the file is self-contained), stock, Face / 2D Pocket / Drill with generated toolpaths, and the posted `first-part.nc`. Built end-to-end through the MCP server; verify is clean; it round-trips through File > Open.

**`docs/images/first-part-*.png`** - four tutorial step pictures that are golden files, not hand-captured screenshots. The docs test in `crates/ui/tests/gpu_render.rs` opens the project through the real open command, steps through `operation_order`, and renders each step with the real viewport pipelines and the real toolpath display (`interact::toolpath_lines`). A normal run compares and fails on drift; `UPDATE_DOCS_IMAGES=1` regenerates - same workflow as the kittest snapshots.

Notes:
- The test lives in the existing `gpu_render` binary on purpose: it shares that binary's GPU lock and adds no new test process (a fifth process racing fallback-device creation across processes is what makes full-suite runs flake).
- While in there, the binary now renders every frame on one shared `OnceLock` device instead of one per frame - the per-frame create/teardown churn was the flake hazard; readbacks are identical and the binary got ~3.5x faster.
- `interact::toolpath_lines`: `pub(crate)` -> `pub` so the test draws through the app's own path display.

Test stability: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --test gpu_render` is 10/10 across repeated runs and deterministic through a regen/compare round-trip. The full-suite wgpu flake is pre-existing on `main` (untouched baseline crashed 3 of 4 runs on this machine) and unrelated to this change.

Keeping this draft until the open questions in #291 are answered - images can move to `docs/guide/src/images/` when the mdbook scaffold lands.

title: feat(app): raise fixture-striking links and retracts over the steel
body:
Was stacked on #476 (#339 slice 1, fixture mesh), which merged on 2026-11-09; this PR now targets main alone. Slice 5 of #339 per the triage on the issue: link and retract routing around fixtures.

## What changed
New `crates/app/src/operation/fixture_route.rs`, with one hook in `generate.rs` before the verify pass. It runs for upright mill paths only.

**The rule:**
- **What a link is:** the longest run of straight rapids between two non-rapid moves, or a path end.
- **When it counts as struck:** the gate's own fixture laws flag it. That's #464's whole-stack law (d2) plus #476's mesh acquittal, so a routed link is judged exactly as the post gate will judge it.
- **The fix:** a struck link becomes three G0 moves: up at its start XY, across, down to its end. The height is the higher of the link's own top and the highest box top under the traverse plus 5 mm (`ROUTE_GAP`). "Under the traverse" means every box the widest band reaches along the XY segment.
- **The cap:** the machine's stated Z stroke (WCS origin Z plus the top of the stroke), keeping at least 0.5 mm over the steel. Steel taller than that **refuses generation by name**: "the link at moves i..j … cannot clear fixture 'Clamp1': its steel stands to Z …, and the machine's Z stroke tops out at Z …". With no stroke stated there is no cap, as everywhere else.
- **Re-judging:** the re-laid link is judged again. If it's still struck, the steel stands over the link's own end column and no height helps. The link is then left as laid, its `FixtureHit` still blocks the post by name, and a path note says why.
- **Notes:** every raised link gets a path note: how many rose, from where, over which fixture, to what Z.

**Left as today (report-only):**
- **Keep-down feed links.** In the CL stream they look exactly like cuts, so lifting one could silently skip a cut. They're only taken inside the cut area, so if one hits steel the cuts beside it hit too, and the post is refused anyway. A keep-down **rapid** run at depth does become retract, traverse and plunge.
- **Other paths:** posed and rotary paths, lathe tools, paths with canned cycles (a traverse inserted between holes could post as a drill), thread or probe records, and runs inside a compensated span.

**Posted G-code changes only** for documents with a link the fixture laws strike, and only those links' G0 moves. Documents without fixtures return early untouched, and links that already clear are never rewritten, so all goldens are unchanged.

`docs/decisions/339-fixture-routing.md`

## How tested
- **New app `fixture_route`** (6 tests):
  - A Contour around two blocks with a strap clamp to Z 40 between them, at clearance 25. As generated, the gate refuses ("strikes a fixture"). After the fix, the links rise to Z 45, the post is clean, the cuts are identical, and the note names Clamp1.
  - A clamp the links already clear leaves the path byte for byte.
  - A 100 mm Z stroke still routes over the 40 mm clamp, while a 400 mm clamp refuses generation naming 'Clamp1' and "Z 400.000".
  - A stay-down rapid link becomes retract, traverse and plunge. Clear steel and no steel are untouched.
  - Steel over a link's own end is left as laid and said.
  - A ceiling under the steel refuses, and a ceiling over it caps the rise.
- **Existing suites keep their verdicts:** fixtures (14), fixture_mesh (3), fixture_law_gaps (3), posting (17), tool_body (8). All app test binaries passed in the quick gate.
- `clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
This changes posted G-code (raised G0 links) for documents with struck fixtures, so it's a draft until a Hub or machine run. It needs a project with a clamp between features.

Changelog: Links and retracts that would strike a fixture are raised over the steel (a clamp taller than the machine's Z stroke refuses generation by name) instead of only being reported (#339)

Refs #339

title: feat(setup): pick the work offset (G54-G59) a setup posts at
body:
## What changed

A setup now picks the work offset its program runs in (G54..G59), builds on #325 (merged).

- **Storage:** `SetupDef.work_offset: Option<usize>`. `None` = **Auto**, the inferred per-operation law every older document posted with (first slot the op's heights reference, else G54). New setups also start on Auto, so existing fixtures and goldens post byte-identically.
- **One law:** `posting::wcs_slot::wcs_slot(world, setup, params)` reads the setup's pick first. `wcs_context` and all of its callers follow it (generation, stamp, spindle law, machine travel check, single-file / per-op / script post, the #315 rotation clause).
- **Command:** `SetSetupWorkOffset`, undoable and validated at construction (setup exists, slot < 6, not the current value). A datum transfer copies the source's pick.
- **UI:** the Setups page has a "Work offset" combo under each setup (Auto, G54..G59). It queues the command and never writes the world itself.
- **Project v51:** the setup payload carries `"work_offset": "G55"`, left out when nothing is picked. v50 files step up with absent = Auto. An unknown word is a corrupt file. The version bump makes older readers refuse the file instead of posting a G55 setup at G54.
- **Refusals by name:**
  - In the verification gate: an op whose heights are measured from a different slot than its setup's pick (`Face1: its heights are measured from G56 but setup Setup1 posts at G55 - ...`).
  - In the one-file / script post: two setups posting the same word from different placements (`setups Setup1 and Setup2 both post at G54 from different placements ... pick another work offset for Setup2 ..., or post one file per operation`). Per-op files are exempt because each file belongs to one setup.
  - Note: the one-file refusal also catches documents that pick nothing. Before this change they posted that case silently.
- **Setup sheet:** WCS OFFSETS ends with `program offset: G55 (picked for this setup)` or `program offset: per operation - ... (not picked)`.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/196-setup-wcs.md`

## Readings

- A G55 pick at (10, 20, 5) gives the same program as G54 at the origin except for the G-word and the coordinates. Every X/Y/Z in the program (not counting the G28 home lines) shifts by exactly (-10, -20, -5).
- Milling stamps do not read the program origin, so a pick leaves milling paths fresh. Turning kinds go stale through the spindle-origin stamp (#62), as they did before.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/setup_wcs.rs` (new, 7 tests):
  - `a_picked_offset_posts_its_word_and_moves_coordinates_by_exactly_the_offset`
  - `the_pick_undoes_and_redoes_exactly`
  - `a_datum_transfer_carries_the_pick`
  - `the_pick_round_trips_and_old_files_read_the_inferred_law`
  - `a_height_on_another_slot_than_the_pick_is_refused_by_name`
  - `two_setups_on_one_word_from_different_placements_refuse_one_file`
  - `the_setup_sheet_names_the_program_offset`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/setup_wcs_tests.rs`:
  - `the_picker_sets_the_setups_work_offset_through_the_command`: kittest; combo click, G55, then Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y.
  - `a_refused_pick_changes_nothing_and_says_why`
- `probe_op`: the version pin is updated from 50 to 51.

## Quick gate (local, debug)

- **App suites, all green:** posting, setups, wcs_align, project_roundtrip, commands_undo, conformance, golden_cl (goldens unchanged), fanuc_post, rotated_wcs, setup_sheet, probe_op, lathe_spindle_law, machine, per_op_files, scripting, setup_wcs, plus the app lib.
- **UI lib (CWD crates/ui):** 287 tests, all green. No snapshot changed: the picker only draws on a document that has setups.
- **Clippy:** `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

Changelog: A setup picks its work offset (G54-G59, default Auto = inferred per operation) on the Setups page; every op of the setup posts at it, the setup sheet names it, and conflicting picks are refused by name (project v51)

Fixes #196

title: feat(kernel): union/intersect and edge blends on the kernel seam, benched (M12.1 stage 2)
body:
M12.1 stage 2 of the Solidcore retirement gate. Stage 1 (68efb11) put solidcore 1.0.1 (tangency-labs' Apache-2.0 pure-Rust port of NVIDIA's SMLib) behind a `Kernel` seam in `camcraft-kernel`, with truck as the reference impl, and benched subtract and offset. This PR adds **union, intersection and edge blends (round/chamfer)** to the seam and the bench. **No production path is switched**: nothing outside `camcraft-kernel` depends on it.

## What changed
- `Kernel` trait: `boolean_union`, `boolean_intersect`, `blend_edges(solid, picks, radius, Blend::Round | Chamfer)`. truck implements union/intersect through truck-shapeops `or`/`and`. Its `blend_edges` returns `Unsupported` (truck has no fillet), and a test asserts that.
- `src/solidcore_blend.rs` (new): picks resolve to edges (256 samples plus golden-section refinement, `PICK_TOL` 1e-3). A pick on two edges at once (a vertex, or a point on a cylinder's seam) is refused as ambiguous. Then the port's `fillet_edges`, followed by a result law: a manifold solid, inside the source box, whose volume actually moved.
- Seam guards: face-less boolean operands are refused (the port returns the **whole box** for `box & empty`, now pinned). The blend radius guard is conservative on purpose (decision 4).
- `tests/common/mod.rs` holds the shared `Want`/`verdict`. Stage 1's 8 tests are all kept, and the count goes to 16.

## Agreement numbers (debug, default tolerances: truck mesh 1e-3 + boolean 1e-2)
| fixture | solidcore abs. error vs closed form | truck abs. error | cross gap (default) | cross gap (heavy lane, 10x finer) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| box-union-box-corner (1875) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| box-union-cylinder-boss (1000+20π) | 2.6e-9 | 1.7e-2 | 1.7e-2 | 2.9e-3 |
| box-intersect-box-corner (125) | 2.8e-14 | 0 | 2.8e-14 | 2.8e-14 |
| box-intersect-cylinder (40π) | 7.6e-9 | 3.4e-2 | 3.4e-2 | 5.7e-3 |
| (stage 1) cylinder-through-box / blind-pocket | 2.8e-8 / 4.2e-8 | 3.4e-2 / 2.6e-2 | same | 5.7e-3 / 2.8e-3 |

All bounding boxes agree within 1.5e-5 (truck's chord), and solidcore's within 1e-14.

Blends (solidcore only, checked against closed forms at 1e-6 relative; **truck: not yet - no blend in truck**):
| fixture | abs. error |

title: feat(ui): machined mesh paints deviation classes and lights the hovered facet
body:
## What changed

The machined mesh in the viewer's stock slot (M13.1) now shows two things it did not before:

- **Deviation classes on the mesh.** Each facet is judged once per mesh, using the same rule the GPU eye uses: the model's `DistanceLattice` (`pack_target`) is read at the facet centroid, with the gate `gate_tol(DEV_TOL, view cell)`. The result is one of four classes: clean, rest, gouge or unjudged. The code is in the new `app::machined_classes` module. The classes are cached in `stock_export::MeshCache` (`classify` / `viewed_classes`) and computed in `ui::machined::prime` alongside the extraction. `world::collect_parts` expands them into the stock part's per-vertex class buffer, so the mesh uses the sheet's and the eye's legend colours. Nothing is computed per frame, and the STL export path does not pay for the classes.
- **Hovered facet highlight.** When the mesh answers a stock hover, `machined::filter_hit_facet` returns the triangle the ray hit. It is stored in `State::hover_mesh`, which is view state, not a command, and is cleared on every hover refresh. The shell draws it as a yellow translucent fill with an outline in the hover colour, projected through the camera each frame, so moving the pointer causes no GPU re-upload. If no mesh stands, or a corner projects behind the camera, nothing is drawn.

The extractor is unchanged. The sim crate is untouched, apart from public items it already exported.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/25-mesh-hover-deviation.md`.

## Results

- Faced fixture (12x12x20 box faced to z 18 over a 12x12x18 model): every up-facing facet on the faced top classifies clean. The class buffer has the same length as the vertex buffer, and only the four class values appear.
- A second `prime` reuses the same classes `Arc`, so nothing is judged twice.

## Tests

- `app::machined_classes::tests`: `the_boundaries_belong_to_clean`, `no_number_no_verdict` (NaN, infinite readings and a NaN tolerance give unjudged; nothing panics), `no_target_paints_every_facet_unjudged`, `facets_on_above_and_under_the_model_class_as_such`.
- `ui::machined_tests`: `nothing_before_a_view_and_one_extraction_after` (now checks the classes, which were previously asserted to be empty), `the_hovered_mesh_facet_is_the_one_the_ray_hit_and_projects`.
- `scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick` fell back to the batch set, and every step passed: geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion and app suites, the ui suites run from `crates/ui`, and clippy with `-D warnings` (19.5 min). No snapshots changed.

Not hand-tested in the GUI yet.

Changelog: The machined stock mesh paints the Deviate classes (clean / rest / gouge / unjudged) and highlights the facet under the pointer.

title: feat(multiaxis): continuous C-axis live tooling - stated C on cl moves, the C word in the lathe post
body:
Continuous C-axis live tooling, first shippable slice: the rotary kinds (Rotary Contour / Parallel / Offset) on a mill-turn whose spindle is C now generate, verify and post through the Fanuc lathe post, instead of refusing "pinned (M13.5 B)".

## What changed

- **cl**: `Move::rotary: Option<f64>`, the spindle's stated C in unwrapped degrees, beside the part-frame `to`/`axis`. `cl::stamp_c` (new `cl/rotary.rs`) stamps a radially posed part-frame path: C = minus the tip's azimuth (Rz(C) turns the tip onto the +X live-tool station), unwrapped move to move. Every move is split collinearly until the machine's X/Z/C-linear motion follows the verified chord within the op's tolerance. Refused by name: arcs, moves with no pose or a pose off the radial station, moves it cannot split near the spindle line, and paths carrying cycle/comp/thread/probe records. When the field is absent nothing changes: goldens, streams and project files stay byte-identical (the project field skips serialization).
- **app**: the rotary letter gate now returns 'C' for the spindle line, and the three rotary arms stamp their path (`rotary_gate::stamp_spindle_c`, the line must be world Z). `machine::check_document` checks a C move for a rotary named C and its stated travel, and no longer reads the part-frame axis as A/B for it. `MoveDto.rotary` persists the angle.
- **post stream/engine**: a C path writes `PARAM LiveTool radial` and `A 0 B 0 C <c>` on every move. The engine refuses that section by name for any script that does not declare `liveTooling = true` (same pattern as `coolantModes`), so every mill post refuses it.
- **.mch grammar**: `tool_station.live_tool { c_axis_on, c_axis_off, spindle_on, spindle_off }`, the builder-specific engage and live-spindle words (all four or none), mirrored to `machine.liveTool`.
- **fanuc-lathe.cps**: the C section. G98, the machine's C-on word, `<spindle_on> S<rpm>`. Every move is turned by C and must land on the station (5 um), otherwise it is refused and never projected. Output is `G01 X<2r> Z C F`, with F scaled for the control's composite rotary feed law (C degrees counted as mm). Rapids are G01 at the machine's stated max feed, never G00. The first move positions with `G00 C` and then `G00 X Z`. Arcs and cycles in the section are refused. Afterwards: spindle off, C off, G99. With no `live_tool` words stated, the section is refused by name.

## Readings

- The wrapped helix golden at r10, 30 deg chords, tol 0.01: each chord splits into 8 pieces. X dips to 19.318 at the chord midpoints, so the tool follows the planned chord, not an arc. F is about 2250-2370 for a 400 mm/min tip feed (composite degree-as-mm scaling).
- The Rotary Contour on the standing r6/r5 bar (mill-turn C) generates with every move on the station, posts with zero warnings, and contains no M03.

## Tests

- `cl::rotary::tests::*` (3): unwrap, winding, refusals.
- `c_axis_live.rs` (new, 4):
  - `a_rotary_contour_on_the_spindle_states_c_on_every_move_and_posts`: generate + post.
  - `the_wrapped_helix_posts_to_its_golden`: `golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/c_axis_helix.nc`.
  - `every_post_without_c_or_without_the_machines_words_refuses_by_name`: mill post / no live_tool words / C disagreeing with XY.
  - `the_c_word_rides_the_stream_and_parses_back`: also proves a path without C stays byte-shape identical.
- `rotary_letter.rs`: the pinned test is replaced by `the_mill_turn_spindle_as_c_axis_answers_c_and_stamps_it`. `operation::rotary_gate` unit test updated the same way.
- Touched suites run: see the PR comment for the gate readings.

## Limits (owed on #33, see docs/decisions/33-continuous-c.md)

- The machine C-sense word.
- Unwinding C on links against a stated travel. The shipped millturn.mch states -360..360, so a multi-ring path is refused by the letter gate.
- Axial/face live-tool stations and G12.1 polar interpolation.
- Arcs on a C turn.
- The composite feed law is a stated assumption about Fanuc-style controls, to be confirmed on a real control.
- The shipped millturn.mch states no live_tool words, so in-app posting of a C op refuses by name until the user's machine file states them.
- Size: `post/src/post/mod.rs` (465 -> 483) and `fanuc-lathe.cps` (424 -> ~520) were already over the 400-line target and grew.

Changelog: Continuous C-axis live tooling: rotary kinds on a mill-turn's spindle C state the C angle per move, split to tolerance, and post through the Fanuc lathe post (X Z C under G98 with the machine's live_tool words); every post without liveTooling refuses by name

title: build(wasm): camcraft-app links for wasm32 via a pinned wasi-sysroot (#31 rung 1)
body:
Rung 1 of the app/UI-on-wasm work. **This is a partial PR**: the domain layer builds and links for wasm32. The UI does not yet.

## What builds
- `web/build-app-wasm.sh` builds `camcraft-app` for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and links `camcraft-cli.wasm`. That covers flecs' C, boa, truck, clipper2 and rayon. Before this, only geometry, cl and post compiled for wasm32.
- flecs' C needs a libc, and this target has none. The script downloads the wasi-sysroot 34 tarball, checks its sha256, and passes its headers through `CFLAGS_wasm32_unknown_unknown`. It also adds `-D__COSMOCC__` (flecs' generic-POSIX path) and `-D__wasi__`. At link time its `libc.a` resolves malloc, printf, pthread, clock and the rest.
- flecs_ecs 0.2.2 and flecs_ecs_sys 0.2.1 do not compile for wasm32 as published; upstream says that support is still in progress. The script copies both crates and makes three edits to the copies:
  - `libc::FILE` becomes `c_void`.
  - The pre-generated bindings use `"C"` in place of `"C-unwind"`.
  - meta_fn_types' wasm-gated `WorldRef`/`Entity` import is no longer gated.

  The copies are used through `cargo --config patch.crates-io...` for this build only. Each edit checks that its patch point is still there, so a flecs bump that moves one fails the build instead of passing silently. The tracked `Cargo.lock` is restored when the script exits.
- The `wasm` job in `ci.yml` now runs the script. Like every job in that file it is `workflow_dispatch` only, so it adds no push, PR or schedule trigger.
- No Rust source, manifest or lock file changed, so the native build is unchanged.

## Readings
- Local run (Windows, Git Bash, clang 21.1.8): `web/build-app-wasm.sh` finished in 2m52s and printed `linked .../wasm32-unknown-unknown/debug/camcraft-cli.wasm` (270 MB, debug). Afterwards `git status` was clean, which shows the lock was restored.
- The linked module has two groups of imports:
  - the wasm-bindgen placeholders;
  - nine `wasi_snapshot_preview1` functions: `clock_time_get`, `fd_close`, `fd_fdstat_get`, `fd_prestat_get`, `fd_prestat_dir_name`, `fd_seek`, `fd_write`, `poll_oneoff`, `proc_exit`.
- I have not run the CI job. It is manual and the Actions budget applies.

## What does not build yet, and why (#31 stays open)
`cargo build -p camcraft-ui --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, with the flecs patches applied, stops at:
```
error[E0407]: method `bytes` is not a member of trait `egui::DroppedFile`
  --> egui-winit-0.36.2\src\dropped_file.rs:19:5
error[E0046]: not all trait items implemented, missing: `bytes_async`
error: could not compile `egui-winit` (lib) due to 2 previous errors
```
egui-winit 0.36.2 is native-only, so the browser shell needs eframe's web runner in its place. After that, the following are still owed; details are in `docs/decisions/31-wasm-ui.md`:
- Move `shell_layout` out of `shell.rs` so both shells call it.
- Bring up the GPU asynchronously. About ten `pollster::block_on` sites remain.
- Replace the synchronous `rfd::FileDialog` (9 sites) with an async version or an `<input type=file>` seam.
- Add a `web_time` seam for `std::time::Instant`, which panics on this target.
- Run work inline where the code calls `std::thread::spawn`.
- Write a JS shim for the nine wasi imports.
- Pin wasm-bindgen CLI 0.2.129.

## Tests
No Rust code changed, so there are no new pinning tests. The proof is the script itself, run locally above. `bash -n web/build-app-wasm.sh` passes.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/31-wasm-ui.md`.

Changelog: none (build tooling only; there is no user-visible change until the UI rung lands)

title: build: Docker builds for the shipped Linux target (and documented cross/native rules)
body:
## What changed

A `docker/` directory (local tooling - no workflow, no Actions minutes) with a per-target answer for every release.yml asset:

| Shipped target | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Linux x86_64 tar.gz / deb / rpm / AppImage | `docker/linux.Dockerfile`: `ubuntu:22.04` pinned by digest (runner distro, glibc 2.35), release.yml's apt list verbatim (+ `build-essential ca-certificates curl file`, preinstalled on the runner, absent in a bare image), the same `cargo build --locked --release -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post`, `scripts/package-linux.sh` + `scripts/package-appimage.sh` with the same pinned linuxdeploy URL and SHA-256, and the job's package-content checks. Rust pinned by `RUST_TOOLCHAIN` build arg (default 1.99.1). `--output type=local,dest=dist` writes the four packages to the host. AppImage needs no FUSE (the script only `--appimage-extract`s linuxdeploy). |
| Snap, Flatpak | Stay on the runner jobs: snapcraft needs snapd, flatpak-builder needs bwrap namespaces - both mean a `--privileged` container. Documented. |
| Windows zip + Inno installer (msvc) | Stays native: msvc target, ISCC.exe and signtool are Windows-only; cargo-xwin would bake Microsoft's CRT/SDK into an image. Documented. |
| Windows (unofficial) | `docker/windows-gnu.Dockerfile`: mingw-w64 cross build of `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`, portable zip with the release layout named `-win-x64-gnu.zip` so it is never mistaken for a release asset. |
| macOS universal zip / dmg | Stays on `macos-15`: Apple SDK licensed for Apple hardware only, `hdiutil` is macOS-only. Documented. |

Also: `docker/build.sh` (`linux` / `windows` / `all`), root `.dockerignore` (keeps `target/`, `dist/`, `.git`, `.claude/`, `graphify-out/` out of the context), a pointer in `scripts/README.md`, decision in `docs/decisions/30-docker-builds.md`.

## Verification - what was and was not exercised

- **Docker is not installed on this dev box** (`docker: command not found`; only a leftover `docker-desktop` WSL distro with no daemon). **Neither image has been built.** hadolint is not installed either, so the Dockerfiles are unlinted.
- Linux Dockerfile checked by hand line by line against release.yml's linux job (apt list, cargo line, linuxdeploy URL + SHA-256, package checks). Base digest fetched from Docker Hub's registry for `ubuntu:22.04` today.
- Windows gnu: the dependency question was tested natively - `cargo build --locked --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui` with MSYS2 mingw64 gcc **succeeded** (4m15s; flecs C sources compile under mingw, wgpu/winit/rfd link). `post.exe --version` -> `post 0.14.0`, `camcraft-cli.exe --help` runs. The GUI was not launched. Not exercised: Ubuntu 22.04's older mingw-w64 (gcc 10) inside the container.
- `bash -n docker/build.sh` passes; the Cargo.toml version `sed` in the Windows image returns `0.14.0`.
- First real `docker/build.sh all` on a Docker host is the remaining check before marking ready.

No Rust code changed; no test suites apply.

Changelog: Docker builds: `docker/linux.Dockerfile` rebuilds the Linux tar.gz/deb/rpm/AppImage in a container, `docker/windows-gnu.Dockerfile` cross-builds an unofficial Windows zip; README names why snap, Flatpak, the msvc Windows build and macOS stay on their runners

title: feat(sim): the hidden-rest scan answers past its holding budget
body:
## What changed

Past the 1.2 M-cell / 40 M-claim budgets, the hidden-rest scan (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/scan_hidden.rs`) used to read `RestUnjudged` ("NOT JUDGED") and block the post. It now gives a real verdict there:

- **Streamed in row bands.** `cells` / `claims` now cap what one pass *holds* at once (the bins, ~1.6 GB at 40 M claims), not what the verdict can read. When a lattice doesn't fit, its claims are counted row by row, the rows are cut into bands that fit, and each band is judged by the **same** body. Every column sees the same claims, pairing and distance law, so the banded verdict matches the whole-lattice verdict bit for bit (rows go in ascending order and a tie keeps the first worst). Nothing is sampled coarser, because a skipped column could hide a ledge and a false clean is a gouge-class bug.
- **Bounded work.** `ScanBudget` gains `work` (shipped 1 G facet-column visits plus ball-center distances, about 10 s at worst). The scan still answers `OverBudget` / NOT JUDGED by name past that limit, or when a single row's claims cannot be held. It never hangs and never reports a stated zero.
- **Exact nearest-center query** (`scan_near.rs`, new). A uniform XY grid over the center path, walked ring by ring outward. The walk stops on the ring's XY lower bound combined with the path's Z-range gap. The previous query's segment is tried first. A top is let go early only when it provably cannot raise the worst rest, so the minimum is the same number a linear scan returns.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/24-field-scan-verdict.md`. A coarse lattice was dropped because it is not conservative. Per-column SDF parity was dropped because it costs O(columns x facets).

## Readings

- 21-plate stack over 100 x 100 mm, r = 0.5 ball: 1.07 M columns and 44.0 M claims, which is past the shipped 40 M. **Before:** NOT JUDGED. **After:** judged, 41.206 mm hidden rest at the deepest plate top between two passes (hypot(10, 40.5) - 0.5, as expected). In release the verdict takes 14.5 s, of which 2.2 s is everything except the hidden half.
- Ceiling fixture streamed at a 600-claim budget (it holds about 4096 claims): rest and location identical to the whole scan, bit for bit.

## Pinning tests

`crates/sim/tests/hidden_rest_banded.rs`:
- `past_the_claim_budget_the_hidden_slab_is_still_found`: the hidden rest is found while streaming.
- `past_the_cell_budget_the_bands_answer_too`
- `a_small_hidden_ledge_in_one_band_is_not_skipped`: a localized ledge is found with tight bands.
- `a_clean_flat_stays_clean_when_streamed`: the clean case.
- `the_walk_stays_bounded_and_says_so`: the work cap still refuses by name.
- `a_stack_past_the_shipped_budget_gets_a_real_verdict`: `#[ignore]` heavy lane (release). The 44 M-claim model under `ScanBudget::SHIPPED`, with a time bound.

`crates/sim/tests/stock_sim.rs::hidden_rest_over_budget_says_not_judged` is updated: it now starves a single row (claims, cells) or the work budget.

## Gate

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- All camcraft-sim suites in debug: green.
- camcraft-motion `finish3d`, `flow`, `pivot5d`, `turning_blade`, `turning_form`, `turning_thread`: green.
- camcraft-app `posed_contact`, `turning_form`, `turning_thread`, `verify`: green.
- Release heavy lane: `hidden_rest_banded --ignored` green, motion `finish3d --ignored` 33/33 green (60.6 s).

Changelog: The hidden-rest scan gives a real verdict past its 1.2 M-cell / 40 M-claim budget (streamed in row bands, same verdict bit for bit); only its new work budget still reads NOT JUDGED

Fixes #24

title: feat(sim): dual contouring for the machined-stock mesh
body:
## What changed

Dual contouring (Ju, Losasso, Schaefer & Warren, "Dual Contouring of Hermite Data", SIGGRAPH 2002) for the machined-stock mesh, on the same cell-centre samples marching tetrahedra reads.

- `stock_sim::iso`: sampling split out into a shared `Grid`; new `IsoMethod { Dual (default), Marching }` and `extract_with(field, step, method)`. `extract` / `extract_at` (the STL export and the viewer's `MeshCache`) now return the dual mesh. A dual mesh with any open edge is never returned: the marching mesh of the same samples stands in, and that is logged.
- `stock_sim::dual` (new): one QEF vertex per sign-changing cell, one quad per sign-changing lattice edge, wound from material to air.
- `stock_sim::hermite` (new): the Hermite data. Normals come from the slope of the crossing sheet across the parallel edges beside each crossing; the sampled gradient is the fallback. A crossing next to a ridge is marked untrusted (|va|+|vb| < 0.95·h·|n_k|), and a cell holding one solves from the trusted, same-facing planes of its 3x3x3 block instead.
- `stock_sim::qef` (new): a pseudo-inverse with singular values under 0.1 of the largest dropped, so an ill-conditioned direction keeps the mass point. The vertex is clamped into its own cell, a non-finite answer falls back to the mass point, and the Jacobi eigensolver has a sweep cap.
- `docs/decisions/23-dual-contouring.md`: why dual is the default (an API parameter, not a user op parameter) and why the plain-gradient normals were dropped.

## Readings (cell 1.0)

| fixture | dual | marching | truth |
|---|---|---|---|
| slot floor/wall edge, worst gap to the mesh | **0.0000** cells | 0.3606 cells | 0 |
| 10x8x6 box volume | **480.000** | 472.307 | 480 |
| ball-nose pocket volume | 949.775 | 948.013 | 957.458 |

Plain central-difference gradient normals gave a 0.35-cell corner gap, no better than marching. That is why the sheet-slope and trusted-plane estimators exist.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/sim/tests/stock_dual.rs`: `dual_contouring_keeps_the_slot_floor_wall_edge_sharp` (dual < 0.05 cell, marching > 0.2 cell, both closed), `dual_is_the_default_extractor`, `a_fully_cut_field_extracts_nothing_without_error`, `a_body_under_one_cell_never_panics_and_never_opens`, `a_curved_ball_pocket_stays_closed_and_never_bulges`.
- Unit tests: `qef::tests::*` (corner, edge, ill-conditioned/empty/NaN, far intersection clamped), `dual::tests::*` (empty lattice, single cell, NaN and truncated lattice).

## Gate

- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim`: every suite green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `camcraft-app --test stock_export` (2/2), `camcraft-ui --lib machined` (2/2), `camcraft-ui --test gpu_render machined_mesh_paints_as_stock` (1/1): green.

Changelog: The machined-stock mesh (STL export, viewer) is extracted by dual contouring by default, so a pocket's sharp floor/wall edge survives where marching tetrahedra rounded it off; marching remains as the fallback and as a named method.

Fixes #23

title: feat(build): a headless binary per crate
body:
Each library crate now ships a small headless CLI, shaped like `post` (a `USAGE` text, `--help`, `--version`, hand-rolled arguments, no new dependency). Bad input exits 1 with a `<bin>: <message>` line and never panics.

| binary | does |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-geometry <model.stl>` | reads binary or ASCII STL and prints triangles, bounds, size, degenerate facets, open edges, closed |
| `camcraft-cl <file.cl>` | reads a CL dump and prints move counts by kind, arcs, cycles, rapid and cut length, bounds, chaining (exits non-zero if the moves do not chain) |
| `camcraft-tools list` / `speeds <work> <tool-mat> <D> <z>` | lists the built-in catalog with its sanity check; prints the rpm and feed window from the cutting table |
| `camcraft-sim <file.cl> x0 y0 z0 x1 y1 z1 <D> [--ball] [--cell]` | cuts a stock box on the dexel grid and prints removed volume plus a rapid/depth verdict (exit 2 when flagged) |
| `camcraft-motion face [-o f] x0 y0 x1 y1 <D> <stepover> <cut-z> <clear-z>` | runs the facing generator over a rectangle and writes a CL dump |

New module `cl::text`: a reader and writer for the golden CL dump grammar. Until now the writer lived only in app's test helpers and the reader only inside post, so cl, sim and motion could not reach either. Its output matches the golden writer byte for byte.

Layering holds: no bin depends on app or ui. The sim change is limited to a new `src/bin` file and its test. The binaries are **not** added to the release zip (decision in `docs/decisions/32-headless-bins.md`).

**Tests** (`tests/headless_bin.rs` in each crate, run through `CARGO_BIN_EXE_*`):
- geometry: `geometry_bin_reads_a_closed_cube`, `geometry_bin_reads_ascii`, `geometry_bin_refuses_bad_input` (missing, garbage, truncated, NaN, unterminated facet, no args)
- cl: `cl_text_round_trips_every_golden` (every `crates/app/tests/golden/*.cl` is read and written back byte for byte), `cl_bin_prints_move_stats`, `cl_bin_refuses_bad_input`
- tools: `tools_bin_lists_a_sane_catalog`, `tools_bin_computes_speeds`, `tools_bin_refuses_bad_input`
- sim: `sim_bin_removes_a_slot` (volume within 3% of analytic), `sim_bin_flags_a_rapid_through_stock`, `sim_bin_refuses_bad_input`
- motion: `motion_bin_faces_a_rectangle` (output reads back as a chained path), `motion_bin_refuses_bad_input`

All 14 pass. Also green: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-{geometry,cl,tools,sim,motion} --bins --tests --lib -- -D warnings` and the cl lib unit tests.

Changelog: Headless CLIs per crate: camcraft-geometry, camcraft-cl, camcraft-tools, camcraft-sim, camcraft-motion (dev tools, not in the release zip); cl gains a CL dump reader/writer (`cl::text`).
